17.d:
The engine tuning method.
	
Volumetric Efficiency - Often referred to as VE. It is selected when the Volumetric Efficiency calculation is to be used for Fuel Base table. This will take into account the number of cylinders, engine displacement, engine load, air temperature, fuel density, and the injector flow characteristics. The Fuel Base table values will reflect engine efficiency. The final calculation fuel amount will also take into account the Target Lambda table.

Mass Airflow - Selected when you want to tune with a Mass Air Flow Sensor. The Fuel Base table will be a correction multiplier to the Mass Air Flow calibration curve and tuning will begin with 1.000 for all values. A value of 1.010 will add 1% fuel, a value of 0.990 will reduce fuel by 1%.

Injection Time - Selected when a raw amount of injection time is to be entered into the Fuel Base Table.  Fuel Base table values will be in injection time.

Fuel Flow Rate - Selected when you want to tune by entering desired fuel flow rate into the Fuel Base table. This will take into account the number of cylinders, engine displacement, and the injector flow characteristics. YOu can change between cc/minute, gallons per hour and pounds per hour in the software by changing the Fuel Volume unit, which can be found under Tools->Options.

36.d:
Controls how the fuel or ignition limiting is performed.
 * Hard Cut - An aggressive rpm limiter. All cylinders are cut at the defined RPM Limit and resume operation when the RPM has fallen below the RPM Limit value by the Hysterisis amount.
 * Soft Cut - A softer rpm limiter. Individual cylinders are cut evenly to maintain RPM at or below the RPM Limit.
 * Cut Off - A user defined rpm limiter. A user definable percentage cut with user definable cut pattern (determined by the Adder Value) is used, resulting in smoother or rougher cuts as requested. This can change the sound of the RPM limiter.

37.d: Used only when the Cut Type is set to Hard. After the RPM Limiter has been activated the RPM must fall this amount below the RPM Limit to re-enable the fuel or ignition outputs and resume normal operation.

58.d:
The logic level of the output when it is active (on). The other option becomes the inactive state logic level.

		Low = Driven to 0 Volts. Current Limit: 1 Amp.
		High = Pulled to Pull Up Voltage through a 4k7 Ohm resistor.
	
If output is active (output is 'on'):
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 1.

If output is Inactive (output is 'off'):
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 1.

If your load is connected between a positive voltage source (e.g. battery 12V) and the ECU:
* Active State is usually 0.
* This is sometimes called Low Side Drive or Ground Side Drive or Cold Side Switching.
* This is the most common drive type in EFI systems.

If your load is connected between Ground and the ECU:
* This can only be controlled by DPOs which allow High Side drive or Both.
* Active State is usually 1.
* This is sometimes called High Side Drive or Hot Side Switching.
* This is common in cars which weren't designed for EFI.
* This is used for Honda VTEC.

97.d:
The TDC angle is important to set correctly to ensure ignition timing accuracy. The TDC angle is correct when the commanded ignition advance in the ECU and the actual ignition advance both match. For assistance and information on setting your TDC Angle, see the Help section. 
TDC Angle relates to the physical crank/cam sensor position as follows:
For equally spaced trigger teeth, the TDC angle is the angle between the first Trigger (crank) tooth after the Home (cam) tooth and TDC for cylinder 1 compression. 
For a missing-tooth style trigger, the ECU waits for the Home (cam) tooth, then looks for the missing tooth gap on the Trigger (crank) signal. The TDC angle is the angle from the first Trigger (crank) tooth after the missing tooth gap and TDC compression cylinder 1. 
The TDC angle can be a value between 0 and 720 for 4-stroke engines, and 0-360 for 2 stroke and Rotary engines.

98.d:
The ignition firing mode.
Direct fire - An ignition output per cylinder.
Wasted spark - An ignition output for every two cylinders.
Distributor - One output for all cylinders.
Twin distributor - Two outputs for all cylinders.
Single wire CDI - One output for all cylinders that goes to a CDI unit. IGN2 (4 stroke) or IGN3 (rotary) Outputs are used for CDI Power Mode selection

102.d: The minimum duty cycle an injection stage can run at. If the injection system is running on two stages or more and the duty cycle of the injectors falls below this value then the last stage turned on will turn off.

103.d: The maximum duty cycle an injection stage can run at. If the injection system is running on two stages or more and the duty cycle of the injectors rises below this value then the next stage turned on will turn on.

107.d:
The injection firing mode for stage 1.
	Sequential - Fires each injector once per cycle and its base angle lines up with TDC of its associated cylinder.
	Semi-sequential - Fires each injector twice per cycle and its base angle lines up with TDC of its associated cylinder(s).
	Sequential-Any Sync - Fires each injector once per cycle and its base angle lines up with the TDC of a cylinder, not necessarily its associated one. Works in any sync mode but only with triggers which do not change mode while running.
	Multi-point - Fires each injector the number of times set by this stage's Injection Events Per Engine Cycle setting. All injectors fire at the same time
	Batch - Fires each injector the number of times set by this stage's Injection Events Per Engine Cycle setting. The second half of the injector outputs fire offset from the first half.

136.d:
The very first pulse of fuel when the engine initially cranks and obtains trigger sync. Not used after that has occurred. If tuned correctly it should supply the correct amount of fuel to start the engine on the first attempt with no addition throttle input. Injection Time Mode: The injection time needed for priming the engine.
VE Mode: The percentage of the mass of fuel at 100% V.E. for an engine at rest needed for priming the engine.

138.d: The percentage correction to the fuel amount once the engine has started running. This is used to compensate for fuel that is lost to the port wall and valve rather than making it to combustion during initial startup.

139.d: The percentage correction to the fuel amount across coolant temperature. Typically used to correct for fuel requirements for cold engine running.

140.d: The percentage correction to the fuel amount across air temperature. When the Auto V.E. Auto Air Temp Compensation box is ticked you would start with all zeroes for this table. When it is not ticked you would expect to see positive values at low temperatures and negative values at high temperatures.

143.d: The percentage correction to the fuel amount across barometric pressure.

144.d: The percentage correction to the fuel amount across manifold pressure. This table should not be used when the Base table is already mapped against MAP. It is often used when TPS is used for the Base table. When mapping is via VE there is already a background correction being applied so this table would start with all zeroes. If Injection Time is used then values that are negative under vacuum and positive under boost should be entered.

145.d: Max Mass Air Flow. Values above this are clipped. Often used at low RPM with preventing air flow spikes that occur with sudden throttle opening.

146.d: The rate at which fuel enrichment is applied in response to a transient throttle event. This table is used to proportion the amount of enrichment based on the rate of opening throttle movement and the throttle position you were at when the movement began.

160.d: The dwell time of the ignition pulses.

161.d: The ignition angle that will be output while the RPM is below the Max Cranking RPM value. This table overrides the Ignition Base table.

162.d: This table controls how many degrees of ignition timing correction will be applied based on the time since the engine started, and is often mapped against Engine Running Time and Coolant Temperature. On a forced induction engine, this should be measuring the air temperature after the compressor and inter-cooler.

403.d:
The current ratio of vehicle speed/RPM of the currently selected gear.
Current Gear Ratio is calculated using the best guess of transmission input shaft speed and output shaft speed. 
If you enable the Transmission Input RPM sensor, then that will be used as the input shaft speed. 
Otherwise Engine RPM will be used. 
Transmission Input RPM is better, as it is assumed to be after the clutch or torque converter.

Output shaft speed primarily uses the Vehicle Speed Drive Train sensor, if that is available. 
If not, it will use the average of all driven wheel speed sensors which aren't flagged as an error. 
If no driven wheel speed sensors are available and/or functional, it will use the Vehicle Speed channel.

In order of priority:
If one or both shaft speeds are in error, Current Gear Ratio will read as Error in source channel.
If output shaft speed is stopped (0 km/h / 0 mph) and the input shaft is spinning at least 200 RPM, Current Gear Ratio be 0, as the transmission must be in Neutral.
If one or both shaft speeds are stopped, Current Gear Ratio will set to Condition Not Met.
If none of the above specific conditions are met, then Current Gear Ratio will be calculated as Input Shaft Speed / Output Shaft Speed.

1040.d:
The potential pin states depend on the drive type setting:
Configure which active states exist on the pin.
Low Side: The low state is ground, the high state is open circuit (no connection).
High Side: The low state is open circuit (no connection), the high state is battery voltage.
Both: The low state is ground, the high state is battery voltage.

Setting this setting to low will make the output be in the low state when the output is on and in the high state when the output is off.  When it is set to high it is the inverse of the above.
When it is set to high it is the inverse of the above.

1450.d:
Which state the flat shift control is in. 
For Datalogging and Table purposes Flat Shift States are:
0: Requirements Not Met. Flat Shift has a min RPM and min TPS. No Torque Reduction used.
1: Input Held On. This is to prevent a flat shift occurring immediately when the requirements are met if the switch is on and/or the conditional trigger is active. No Torque Reduction used.
2: Idle. Ready to perform a Flat Shift. No Torque Reduction used.
3: Pulling Out Of Old Gear. Gear Detection indicates that the old gear is still engaged. Full Torque Reduction table values are used. Only used by Closed Loop. Other modes skip it.
4: Shifting. Mid-shift. Full Torque Reduction table values are used.
 - The exit conditions for this state depend on the Flat Shift Mode.
 -- Closed Loop exits this state when Gear Detection detects that it's in the new gear.
 -- While Active exits this state when the input and/or conditions are no longer met.
 -- Timed just checks that the time in this state exceeds the Torque Reduction Time.
 -- Alternately: if the shift time exceeds the Max Shift Time setting.
5: Entering New Gear. Gear Detection indicates that the new gear is now engaged. Torque Reduction will continue for the Torque Reduction Time to allow the new gear to fully engage before entering Recovery state. Full Torque Reduction table values are used. Only used by Closed Loop. Other modes skip it.
6: Recovery. During this phase the Torque Reduction amounts are either immediately stopped or gradually faded out - depending on the Recovery method setting.
7: Post-shift Block-out. Prevents a new shift for the time specified in the Blockout Time setting. No Torque Reduction used.

2409.d:
Gear Type Setting.
	
Gear Ratio: Current Gear Ratio is calculated using the best guess of transmission input shaft speed and output shaft speed. 
If you enable the Transmission Input RPM sensor, then that will be used as the input shaft speed. 
Otherwise Engine RPM will be used. 
Transmission Input RPM is better, as it is assumed to be after the clutch or torque converter.

Output shaft speed primarily uses the Vehicle Speed Drive Train sensor, if that is available. 
If not, it will use the average of all driven wheel speed sensors which aren't flagged as an error. 
If no driven wheel speed sensors are available and/or functional, it will use the Vehicle Speed channel.

In order of priority:
If one or both shaft speeds are in error, Current Gear Ratio will read as Error in source channel.
If output shaft speed is stopped (0 km/h / 0 mph) and the input shaft is spinning at least 200 RPM, Current Gear Ratio be 0, as the transmission must be in Neutral.
If one or both shaft speeds are stopped, Current Gear Ratio will set to Condition Not Met.
If none of the above specific conditions are met, then Current Gear Ratio will be calculated as Input Shaft Speed / Output Shaft Speed.
.
The Current Gear Ratio channel is then compared to the ratios for each gear in the Gear Ratios function.
Whichever gear ratio is closest to the Current Gear Ratio is used as the indicator for what gear the transmission is currently in. 
If the ratio is in error: then the Current Gear channel will go to Unknown, and the Gear channel will remain at it's previous value. 
If the ratio is 0: Then the Current Gear and Gear channels will go to Neutral.

This setting is used as a detection point for Engine Protection if a Fuel Pressure Sensor is installed. 2955.d:
The logic level of the output when it is active (on). The other option becomes the inactive state logic level.

		Low = Driven to 0 Volts. Current Limit: 1 Amp.
		High = Pulled to 12V through a 4k7 Ohm resistor.
	
If output is active (output is 'on'):
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 1.

If output is Inactive (output is 'off'):
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 1.

If your load is connected between a positive voltage source (e.g. battery 12V) and the ECU:
* Active State is usually 0.
* This is sometimes called Low Side Drive or Ground Side Drive or Cold Side Switching.
* This is the most common drive type in EFI systems.

If your load is connected between Ground and the ECU:
* This can only be controlled by DPOs which allow High Side drive or Both.
* Active State is usually 1.
* This is sometimes called High Side Drive or Hot Side Switching.
* This is common in cars which weren't designed for EFI.
* This is used for Honda VTEC.

3261.L: Idle Control Decel Offset Decay Duration
3261.d: This is the amount of time in seconds for the Decel Offset to decay away when the Idle Control conditions are reached after decel. Typically 0.5 to 1.0 seconds.

3285.d: This will add an amount of duty to the Base Duty after the engine has been started. This is to assist Idle Control in reaching the additional RPM added by the Start Target Offset, and is normally mapped to return to zero after a certain amount of time.

3291.d: This is the Delay Time between meeting all of the conditions for closed loop and for it to actually begin correcting the output. This delay is to ensure that the boost pressure has stabilised before trying to making corrections. Typically values around .05 to 2 seconds and is approx the time to get from the Control Point Offset to the Target. data

3296.L: Boost Control Target Offset Pressure Data
3296.d: The controller is inactive while boost is below the target by this amount and will rest on the Base Duty. When Spool Assist is enabled it will rest instead on 100%. Set too high can cause the controller to activate too early and result in control issues. Set too low can cause overshooting when used with the Spool Assist. data

3297.d: The maximum absolute value of the MAP derivative for the Integral portion of the controller to be active. When this value is exceeded the Proportional and Derivative contribution to the Boost control output will still be active, however the Integral value will be reset to zero until the Max Derivative is no longer met. This prevents the Integral from contributing when the rate of change of MAP is too high. i.e. the boost is not stable. This feature is similar to the Controller Delay table and can be used instead of, or together with the Controller Delay table, to ensure stable boost before allowing the controller to make corrections.

3301.d: Shows what amount of correction the closed loop controller is instantaneously making to try and reach the target. Short Term is not stored in memory.

3302.L: Boost Control Long Term Trim Enable
3302.d: Boost Control Long Term Trim will be Enabled if this is ticked.

3303.d: This table shows the amount of Long Term correction that has been learned over time to correct for inaccurate setting of the Base Duty table. The Long Term controller simply reacts to Short Term, so if the Short Term is positive the Long Term will move in a positive direction, and conversely for negative Short Term it will move in a negative direction.

3304.L: Boost Control Long Term Trim Data
3304.d: This table shows the amount of Long Term correction that has been learned over time to correct for inaccurate setting of the Base Duty table. The Long Term controller simply reacts to Short Term. If the Short Term is positive the Long Term will move in a positive direction. Conversely for negative Short Term it will move in a negative direction. data

3305.L: Boost Control Long Term Trim Gain
3305.d: This table control how fast the long term controller reacts to short term correction. A higher number will learn faster but is more prone to oscillation. Typical value is around 50 and often mapped against boost error.

3306.L: Boost Control Long Term Trim Gain Data
3306.d: This table control how fast the long term controller reacts to short term correction. A higher number will learn faster but is more prone to oscillation. Typical value is around 50 and often mapped against boost error. data

3315.d: The boost control output to the solenoid valve will be disabled (0% duty) when boost exceeds the target by this amount. It will remain shut until boost falls back below the target. This is to provide a soft method of overboost control. Typical value is around 30kpa.

3642.L: Boost Control Closed Loop Base Output Data

3660.d: Boost Control Proportional Gain controls how reactive the closed-loop system is to target error. Typical starting point values are around 10 to 30. data

3669.d: Boost Control Integral Gain controls how reactive the closed-loop system is to accumulated error. Typical starting point values are around 50 to 200. data

3678.d: Boost Control Derivative Gain controls how the closed-loop system reacts to overshooting of the target. Typically not used or very low values are used for general boost control use. data

3687.L: Boost Control Output Air Temperature Correction Enable
3687.d: This table allows for correction to the Base Duty for changes in Air Temperature. Typically hotter air requires slightly more duty, and colder air requires slightly less duty.

3688.L: Boost Control Output Air Temperature Correction Data

3717.L: Boost Control Target Pressure Air Temperature Correction Enable
3717.d: This table allows for a Target Boost correction based on the Air Temperature. This is typically used to add an added level of engine safety by allowing the Target Boost to be lowered for excessively hot intake air temperatures if desired.

3718.L: Boost Control Target Pressure Air Temperature Correction Data
3718.d: This table allows for a Target Boost correction based on the Air Temperature. This is typically used to add an added level of engine safety by allowing the Target Boost to be lowered for excessively hot intake air temperatures if desired. data

3723.L: Boost Control Target Pressure Coolant Temperature Correction Enable
3723.d: This table allows for a Target Boost correction based on the Coolant Temperature. This is typically used to add an added level of engine safety by allowing the Target Boost to be lowered for excessively hot Coolant Temperatures or for cold engines if desired.

3724.L: Boost Control Target Pressure Coolant Temperature Correction Data
3724.d: This table allows for a Target Boost correction based on the Coolant Temperature. This is typically used to add an added level of engine safety by allowing the Target Boost to be lowered for excessively hot Coolant Temperatures or for cold engines if desired. data

3729.d: This table allows for a Target Boost correction based on the Gear Position. This is typically used for lowering the Target Boost in the lower gears to assist with traction.

3730.L: Boost Control Target Pressure Gear Correction Data
3730.d: This table allows for a Target Boost correction based on the Gear Position. This is typically used for lowering the Target Boost in the lower gears to assist with traction. data

3735.L: Boost Control Target Pressure Throttle Position Correction Enable
3735.d: This table allows for a Target Boost correction based on the Throttle Position. This is typically used to lower the Target Boost at smaller throttle openings to give the engine a more linear power response to throttle opening.

3736.L: Boost Control Target Pressure Throttle Position Correction Data
3736.d: This table allows for a Target Boost correction based on the Throttle Position. This is typically used to lower the Target Boost at smaller throttle openings to give the engine a more linear power response to throttle opening. data

3741.s: Boost Ctrl Target Flex Fuel Comp Corr En
3741.d: This table allows for a Target Boost correction based on the Ethanol%. This is typically used to increase the Target Boost when there is a higher ethanol percentage in the system for added performance.

3742.L: Boost Control Target Pressure Flex Fuel Composition Correction Data
3742.d: This table allows for a Target Boost correction based on the Ethanol%. This is typically used to increase the Target Boost when there is a higher ethanol percentage in the system for added performance. data

3769.d: If the Narrowband O2 Sensor voltage exceeds this amount it will bypass the Initial Engine Running Time setting and go immediately into closed loop. This allows a warm engine that is restarted to not have to wait this amount of time if the sensor is already at operating temperature. Typically set a little over the Target Voltage, around 0.6V

3803.d: O2 Control Derivative Gain controls the speed of target approach when near to the target and is typically not used for O2 control, but can assist with overshooting issues.

3806.d: O2 control bank 1 source. If bank 2 is disabled O2 control will run in unbanked mode and use this source.

3814.d: This table shows the amount of learned O2 Control Bank 1 Long Term fuel correction. This should typically be mapped to use values that correspond to values used in the Fuel Base table axis. The axis setup for this table will be used also for Bank 2.

3822.L: O2 Control Long Term Fuel Trim Enable
3822.d: This enables the O2 Control Long Term Fuel Trim. This will look at the amount of Short Term O2 Control correction and over a period of time fill out the Long Term Trim table to try and achieve zero correction for the Short Term Trim.

3823.L: Transient Throttle Load Acceleration Dead Band
3823.d: Once a transient throttle enrichment event is triggered, the acceleration of the load source must exceed this value to maintain enrichment. This acts as a Decay system and for longer enrichment periods use a low value, for shorter enrichment periods use a larger value.

3824.d: The acceptable level of oscillation in the target AFR around the desired target.

3827.L: O2 Control Long Term Fuel Trim Rich Bias
3827.d: The enrichment bias of the long term fuel trim map. This is used to allow the long term to learn slightly richer amounts to add an extra level of tuning safety should the system revert to open loop control, perhaps due to sensor failure. The short term control would then correct back to the Target Lambda from this learned bias.

3828.L: O2 Control Long Term Fuel Trim Min Temperature
3828.d: The minimum coolant temperature above which long term fuel trims will activate. This is to prevent the long term table form learning values from a cold engine.

3929.d: Cuts fuel when Decel Detection conditions are met

3930.d: This amount of ignition retard will be fed in over a 500ms period before cutting fuel. If the Delay Time is less than 500ms then this time is shortened to match.

3931.d: This is an amount of enrichment applied when the fuel supply is resumed. This extra fuel is to help with wetting down the dry port walls and should be of sufficient amount to prevent an initial lean condition.

3932.L: Idle Control Closed Loop Activation Offset
3932.d:
This is the offset above target idle that idle control will enter closed loop mode. 
This will override any Decel Min RPM setting if that table is set too low. 
Typically set to at 150 to 200rpm.

3933.L: Decel Cut Post Start Delay Time
3933.d: This prevents Decel Fuel Cut from activating during higher idle speeds seen on Post Start. Typically set to around 5 seconds.

3950.d: The engine RPM must rise this amount above Decel Min RPM table for for the fuel to be again cut. This is to prevent oscillation of the fuel cut. Typically around 300 to 400rpm.

3952.d: Once the enabling condition is no longer met the data logger will continue recording for this amount of time.

3962.L: Transient Throttle Fuel Enrichment Async Amount
3962.d:
This table sets how much additional fuel is delivered during a transient event via asynchronous means, and multiplies with the Enrich Rate table to give a final amount. Typically mapped over RPM.
Asynchronous refers to additional fuel pulses being added between the normal sequential pulses. This is typically set up after the Sync table tuning has been completed.

3969.d:
The minimum amount of positive throttle rate of movement (TPS or MAP Derivative) that is required to trip an Enrichment transient event.
Set too low will cause false activation with unwanted enrichment events
Set too high will cause initial lean spikes due to delayed detection, together with no detection for small throttle movements.
Typically set to 25 to 50%/sec for Throttle.

3970.L: Transient Throttle Fuel Peak Synchronous Output
3970.d: Displays the peak synchronous output value that occurred during the transient throttle event.

3971.L: Transient Throttle Fuel Peak Asynchronous Output
3971.d: Displays the peak asynchronous output value that occurred during the transient throttle event.

3972.L: Transient Throttle Ign Corr Decay Time
3972.d: The time taken for the Transient Throttle Ignition Correction to decay to zero.

3973.d: The battery light output will be on if the battery voltage falls below this level.

3974.L: Drive By Wire Max Throttle Position
3974.d: This is the maximum position the throttle can move to.

3975.d:
In order to calibrate correctly, your vehicle must be travelling at this speed at (and for at least a few seconds after) the time you click on the 'Calibrate' button next to the sensor.

	This is often best achieved on a dyno, or with a GPS speed measuring device.

4001.d: The maximum RPM for which O2 control is active i.e. below this RPM, O2 control is active. This allows an upper RPM limit to be set for closed loop control and is more used for narrowband sensors or for the tuner's own preference.

4006.d:
The minimum amount of negative throttle rate of movement (TPS or MAP Derivative) that is required to trip a Disenrichment transient event.
Set too low will cause false activation with unwanted disenrichment events.
Set too high will cause delayed detection, together with no detection for small throttle movements.
Typically set to -25 to -50%/sec for Throttle.

4007.d: The maximum Throttle Position for which O2 control is enabled. This sets an upper TPS limit above which O2 control disables. This is often used for narrowband sensors or for the tuner's own preference.

4008.d: The maximum Manifold Air Pressure for which O2 control is enabled. This sets an upper MAP limit above which O2 control disables. This is often used for narrowband sensors or for the tuner's own preference.

4023.d: The rate at which fuel disenrichment is applied in response to a lift-off transient throttle event. This table is used to proportion the amount of disenrichment based on the rate of closing throttle movement and the throttle position you were at when the movement began.

4024.d: This table sets how much fuel is removed during a disenrichment transient event (lift-off), and multiplies with the Disenrich Rate table to give a final amount. Typically mapped over RPM. Typical values are 25 to 50 at low rpm, 100 to 200 for high rpm.

4027.L: O2 Control Initial Engine Running Time
4027.d: The amount of time the engine must be running before any O2 control is enabled. This is to allow time for the O2 sensor to reach operating temperature. It will be bypassed if the warm voltage is exceeded or the CAN Widebands are reported as being ready to use.

4028.d: The temperature the coolant must be above before any O2 control is enabled.

4038.L: O2 Control Long Term Fuel Trim Gain
4038.d: O2 Control Long Term Fuel Trim Gain controls the speed at which the Long Term control works. Setting this too high can cause oscillation. Typical values are around 20 to 50.

4039.L: O2 Control Bank 2 Long Term Fuel Trim
4039.d: This table shows the amount of learned O2 Control Bank 2 Long Term fuel correction. The axis values for this table are locked to use the same values as setup for Bank 1.

4053.d: Idle Control will only operate in closed loop when the vehicle speed is below this amount. This setting is to prevent the idle system from making adjustments while the vehicle is not at idle.

4054.L: Idle Control RPM Rate Lower Limit
4054.d: The RPM must be falling at a rate slower than this for the Idle Control to operate in closed loop. This setting is to prevent the idle control from making adjustments to try and reach the Target when the Idle is not yet stable by not operating the Proportional and Integral components. Setting this closer to zero will cause the controller to wait for a steadier RPM before starting the controller. Setting this further from zero will start the controller earlier.

4055.L: Idle Control RPM Rate Upper Limit
4055.d: The RPM must be rising at a rate slower than this for the Idle Control to operate in closed loop. This setting is to prevent the idle control from making adjustments to try and reach the Target when the Idle is not yet stable by not operating the Proportional and Integral components. Setting this closer to zero will cause the controller to wait for a steadier RPM before starting the controller. Setting this further from zero will start the controller earlier.

The RPM must be rising or falling at a rate slower than this for the Idle Control to operate in closed loop. This setting is to prevent the idle control from making adjustments to try and reach the Target when the Idle is not yet stable by not operating the Proportional and Integral components. Setting this closer to zero will cause the controller to wait for a steadier RPM before starting the controller. Setting this further from zero will start the controller earlier.

4056.L: Air Con Idle Up RPM Offset
4056.d: Increases the Idle Target RPM by this amount when engaging the A/C Compressor. This is to allow the engine to develop enough torque to maintain idle quality due to the additional load from the A/C compressor.

4057.L: Air Con Idle Up Duty Cycle Offset
4057.d: Increases the Idle Base Duty when engaging the A/C Compressor to allow the idle to stay on target.

4062.d: The filter level applied to the TPS derivative. TPS-Derivative is used as a rate of change channel for the TPS. Too high can dull response, too low can give unstable readings and false trip the Transient Throttle function.

4079.d: The filter level applied to the MAP derivative. MAP-Derivative is used as a rate of change channel for the MAP sensor. MAP-D is used by the Boost Control when closed loop is the method and a little extra filtering here is often required for consistent operation. Typically set to around 3 to 5.

4123.d: The RPM must exceed this amount of RPM together with the Load and Min Air Temp conditions to activate the Water Injection Output. The output will stay active until the RPM has dropped 1000rpm below this amount.

4129.d: AC output is disabled when the TPS is above this value. This removes the air conditioning compressor load from the engine under high driver demand allowing full power to be delivered.
AC output is disabled when the Engine Demand is above this value. This removes the air conditioning compressor load from the engine under high driver demand allowing full power to be delivered.

4130.d: AC output is disabled when the engine speed exceeds this value. This is to prevent over revving the compressor on some high performance engines and to ensure compressor reliability.

4131.L: Air Con Idle Delay On Time
4131.d: This setting is to allow adequate time for the Idle Control to increase the Target Idle RPM and Base Duty in anticipation of the additional load caused by engaging the A/C clutch. After this time has passed the compressor output is then engaged. Typically around 0.5 seconds.

4132.d: AC output is disabled when the A/C Temperature drops below this value.

4133.d: The A/C Temperature must rise this amount above the Min Temp to re-engage the compressor output.

4135.d: The A/C Pressure must drop this amount below the Max Pressure value to re-engage the A/C output. This is to prevent oscillation.

4137.L: IO Box A Digital Pulse Output 1 Safe State
4137.d:
Allows the user to select the Safe State for DPO1 to be either "Active" or "Inactive" if there is an error with the I/O Expander Box; such as loss in communications with the ECU.
Active - The ECU will activate the output when there is an error. Please check that the Active State has been configured correctly.
Inactive - The ECU will not activate the output when there is an error. Please check that the Active State has been configured correctly. e.g if we are controlling a thermofan relay which is switched on when the Active State is Low we would want the fan to be ON if there is an error. In this case the Safe State would be Active. Alternatively - if we have a Nitrous Solenoid which is switched on when the Active State is Low we would want the solenoid to be OFF if there is an error. In this case the Safe State would be Inactive.

4188.d: Selects which method to arm anti-lag for use. Once it has been armed anti-lag will work when below the Activating Engine Demand. Engine Demand - The Engine Demand must exceed a certain percentage (The Arming Engine Demand) to arm the anti-lag. When the Engine Demand falls below the Activating Engine Demand the anti-lag will run for the time value in Max Time. Switch - When the Engine Demand is below the Activating Engine Demand anti-lag will continue to happen while this switch is on. Engine Demand Switch - This works the same as the Engine Demand option as long as the switch is on.

4190.d:
The Engine Demand value has to be below this threshold for anti-lag to activate.
	If the Intake Air Increase Method is Drive By Wire Throttle Minimum, it is recommended to set this equal to the Intake Air Addition table value when Anti-Lag gets activated. Otherwise there will be an abrupt throttle movement.

4199.d:
Select the type of idle control system that is to be controlled.
BAC Two Wire use a 12V+ and one wire to an ECU Output and is controlled by a duty signal.
BAC Three Wire use a 12V+ and two wires connected to two ECU Outputs and is controlled by a duty signal.
Stepper Wire Relative uses the 4x Stepper Outputs and simply reacts to whether the idle is above or below target.
Stepper Wire Absolute uses the 4x Stepper Outputs and undergoes calibration to know its actual position.
DBW uses a DBW throttle to control the idle.

4201.d: Knock control mode sets whether there is a single or multiple engine banks.

4202.L: Knock Control Short Term Ignition Retard
4202.d: This is the amount of short term retard that is applied when the Knock Detection has seen the Knock Signal exceed the Knock Threshold.

4203.L: Knock Control Long Term Ignition Retard
4203.d: This is the amount of long term retard that will be applied for each knock detection event that occurs in that particular cell.

4204.L: Knock Control Bank 1 Long Term Trim
4204.d: This table is the amount of learned ignition timing correction for the Bank 1 Long Term Trim. Negative numbers are degrees of retard and positive are degrees of advance.

4206.L: Knock Control Bank 2 Long Term Trim
4206.d: This table is the amount of learned ignition timing correction for the Bank 2 Long Term Trim. Negative numbers are degrees of retard and positive are degrees of advance.

4208.L: Knock Control Short Term Decay Rate
4208.d: This is the rate at which the short term correction will decay away back to having no retard. This rate is in how many degrees per Engine Cycle.

4209.L: Knock Control Long Term Trim Enable
4209.d: This enables the ECU to learn over time the amount of ignition timing correct needed to prevent engine knocking.

4210.d: This table controls the amount of fuel correction to be applied while anti-lagging. Additional fuel is sometimes required to assist with producing more exhaust energy to keep the turbo spooled. This table is often mapped against Anti-Lag Trigger Time Remaining and will usually have more fuel towards the right hand side and taper away to no additional fuel by 0 seconds.

4220.d: This table controls the actual ignition timing value that will be used while anti-lagging. It is not a correction. This table is often mapped against Anti-Lag Trigger Time Remaining and will usually have negative timing values (around -20 to -30) towards the right hand side and taper away to positive timing by 0 seconds.

4230.d:
When Intake Air Method is Throttle Bypass Valve this table is simply the duty cycle to use on the output.
When Intake Air Method is Idle Control Offset this table is used as an Idle Control Offset to increase the amount the idle valve is opened. 
When Intake Air Method is Idle Control Minimum this table is used as a minimum value for the Idle Control output. This ensures the valve is sufficiently open. 
When Intake Air Method is Drive By Wire Throttle Minimum this table is the minimum throttle position used. 
Obviously this table is only used while Anti-Lag is active.

4264.d:
Select the method used to arm the Launch Control.
Always On - Launch Control cannot be turned off, it will always be used when conditions are met.
Launch Switch - Launch Control will only operate when the Launch Control Input switch is On.

Brake Switch - Launch Control will only operate when the Brake Switch input is On.
Trans Brake State - Launch Control will only operate when the Trans Brake input is On AND the Trans Brake Enable Condition was met when the input became on. This additional check prevents accidental activation during a pass.

4274.d:
Mode of operation.
Closed Loop: (If available to this ECU) Use full Torque Reduction until the shift is complete. Completion of shift is determined by Gear Detection detecting that the new gear has been reached, then allowing a short extra time for the gearbox to stabilise in the new gear. The extra time is given in the Flat Shift Time table.
Timed: Use full Torque Reduction for a time specified in the Flat Shift Time table.
While Active: Use full Torque Reduction while the input conditions are met.

4453.L: Turbo Timer Engine Run Time Percentage

	If this setting is DISABLED, Engine Run Percentage should be 100%. Eg, when the setting is off, the engine runs for the whole turbo timer time.

5279.d:
This selects which port the Vehicle BUS is on.
			Aux CAN Bus Port is the CAN DTM-4 port directly on the ECU itself inside the cover.
			Main Connectors is the CAN connection via the ECU Connector where the main wiring harness attaches.

5291.L: Transient Throttle Enrichment Load Derivative Max

5292.L: Transient Throttle Disenrichment Load Derivative Min

5295.d: The minimum time required for a transient throttle enrichment event to be triggered. A longer duration will reduce false trips at the cost of a more delayed reaction.

5296.d: The minimum time required for a transient throttle disenrichment event to be triggered. A longer duration will reduce false trips at the cost of a more delayed reaction.

5297.d: Select whether Throttle Position or Manifold Pressure is to be used for Transient Throttle detection. Almost always use Throttle Position.

5298.d: The filter level applied to the TPS. Too high can dull response, too low can give unstable readings and false trip the Transient Throttle function.
The time constant for the filter.  The time taken for a step change on the input to rise ~63% of the way to the full.

5304.L: Boost Control Closed Loop Minimum Throttle Position
5304.d: The closed loop boost control will only adjust the boost control output when the throttle position is above this value. This is to ensure the target is actually achievable and boost is stable.

5305.L: Boost Control Long Term Trim Minimum Throttle Position
5305.d: The Boost control long term trim will only operate above this amount minimum throttle position. This is to ensure the learned values are appropriate for an achievable boost target. Typical value is around 80 to 90%.

5306.L: Boost Control Long Term Trim Minimum RPM
5306.d: The RPM must be above this value for the Long Term Trim to be active. This is typically set to an RPM amount where the Target Boost is actually achievable.

5307.L: Boost Control Long Term Trim Maximum RPM
5307.d: If this RPM is exceeded the Long Term Trim will disable. This is usually set to be a little under the RPM Limit to prevent possibly learning incorrect values while hitting the limiter.

5308.d: This will hold the output at 100% when the manifold pressure is above barometric pressure (positive pressure) and will hold this until the Control Point Offset (Target minus Control Point) pressure is reached, it will then drop the output to the Base Duty amount above this.

5430.d:
How to combine conditions. 
And: The combined result will be true if both individual conditions are true. 
Or: The combined result will be true if at least one individual condition is true.
Note that if you have 3 conditions enabled: And gets evaluated before Or. 
e.g. Cond 1 And  Cond 2 Or Cond 3:
    Cond 1 And Cond 2 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 3. 
e.g. Cond 1 OR Cond 2 AND Cond 3: 
    Cond 2 And Cond 3 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 1.
If both combiners are the same (e.g. both And or both Or): then the order doesn't matter.

5515.d:
Generic output 4 type.

 * Duty Cycle: Set the frequency to be a static value and the duty cycle is controlled using the output table.

 * Frequency: Set the Duty Cycle to be a static value and the frequency is controlled using the output table.

 * State: Set the output to be a state output. State is set by the table. Min Off Time and Min On Time can be set.

 * Current: Configure the output to be current controlled. Target current is the output of the table as a percentage of the maximum current setting of the pin in the wiring page, e.g. 0%-100% of table output is equivalent to 0 amp to Maximum Current setting of the pin.

 * 4-Wire Stepper Position (%): Configure output to control a 4 wire stepper motor. Table output is a target position based on max steps.

 * 6-Wire Stepper Position (%): Configure output to control a 6 wire stepper motor. Table output is a target position based on max steps.

5783.L: Engine Protection Severity Level 1 DTC Active Condition
5783.d:
The DTC active condition used to action severity level 1.

Current and past DTCs :
Severity level will be active while a DTC of the respective severity level has a status of either "Current" or "Past".

Current DTCs Only (Drive cycle):
Severity level will be active if a DTC of the respective severity level has had a status of "Current" in the drivecycle.
A drive cycle is defined as the period of time between turning the ECU on and turning the ECU off.

5965.d:
Speed limit.
Please ensure your Vehicle Speed sensors have been accurately calibrated so that this speed limit works correctly.
This is used to calculate an engine RPM limit which is used to keep your vehicle speed below the limit.
Note that the fastest vehicle speed sensor reading is used. This means that a single sensor failing won't prevent the speed limiter from working. data

6003.d:
Speed difference before the Speed Limiter cut kicks in.
This channel is useful for mapping against things like ignition retard and DBW Maximum.
e.g. it can be mapped so that the DBW max is 100% whenever this channel is more than 20 km/h to allow full driver control and then decrease to 20% when this channel is 0.
While the Speed Limiter is enabled by the driver: this is Speed Limit minus the highest vehicle speed sensor.
When the Speed Limiter is disabled by the driver: this is a very large number (which shows up as Disabled).

6223.d: The minimum RPM for which O2 control is active i.e. above this RPM, O2 control is active. This is to prevent O2 Control from making fuel changes while the engine is cranking.

6224.d: Select whether TPS or MAP is to be used to detect when the engine is decelerating. Typically TPS is used.

6225.d: The manifold pressure below which the engine is considered to be decelerating.

6231.d: The temperature at which Thermofan 4 will switch on.

6232.d: The temperature at which Thermofan 4 will switch off.

6233.d: Enables the thermofan when air conditioning is active.

6234.d: The minimum duty cycle to use when AC is enabled.

6235.d: This setting is to allow adequate time for the Idle Control to increase the idle rpm before activating the thermofan.

6617.L: REM Digital Pulse Output 1 Active State
6617.d:
The logic level of the output when it is active (on). The other option becomes the inactive state logic level.

		Low = Driven to 0 Volts. Current Limit: 1 Amp.
		High = Pulled to Pull Up Voltage through a 4k7 Ohm resistor.
	
If output is active (output is 'on'):
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 1.

If output is Inactive (output is 'off'):
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 1.

If your load is connected between a positive voltage source (e.g. battery 12V) and the ECU:
* Active State is usually 0.
* This is sometimes called Low Side Drive or Ground Side Drive or Cold Side Switching.
* This is the most common drive type in EFI systems.

If your load is connected between Ground and the ECU:
* This can only be controlled by DPOs which allow High Side drive or Both.
* Active State is usually 1.
* This is sometimes called High Side Drive or Hot Side Switching.
* This is common in cars which weren't designed for EFI.
* This is used for Honda VTEC.

6618.d: The period of the signal put out on the REM DPO 1 pin.

6619.L: REM Digital Pulse Output 1 Active Time
6619.d: The active time of the signal put out on the REM DPO 1 pin.

6620.L: REM Digital Pulse Output 1 Safe State
6620.d:
Allows the user to select the Safe State for DPO1 to be either "Active" or "Inactive" if there is an error with the Race Expansion Module; such as loss in communications with the ECU.
	Active - The ECU will activate the output when there is an error. Please check that the Active State has been configured correctly. A thermo-fan is an example of something which should have Active safe state.
	Inactive - The ECU will not activate the output when there is an error. Please check that the Active State has been configured correctly.
	eg. if we are controlling a thermofan relay; which is switched on when the Active State is Low; we would want the fan to be ON if there is an error. Therefore; the Safe State would be Active.
	Alternatively; if we have a Nitrous Solenoid; which is switched on when the Active State is Low; we would want the solenoid to be OFF if there is an error. Therefore; the Safe State would be Inactive.

6754.d:
This is the calculated slip speed.
For Rear Wheel Drive and Front Wheel Drive cars, it is calculated as Driven Wheel Speed - Un-driven Wheel Speed.
For All Wheel Drive cars, it is calculated as fastest wheel speed - slowest wheel speed.

6755.d:
This is the calculated slip rate.
For Rear Wheel Drive and Front Wheel Drive cars, it is calculated as Driven Wheel Speed Derivative - Un-driven Wheel Speed Derivative.
For All Wheel Drive cars, it is calculated as derivative of the fastest wheel speed - derivative of the slowest wheel speed.

6756.d:
This is the calculated slip percentage.
For Rear Wheel Drive and Front Wheel Drive cars, it is calculated as (Driven Wheel Speed - Un-driven Wheel Speed) * 100% / Un-driven Wheel Speed. If Un-driven Wheel Speed is 0, it will show 0% if Driven Wheel Speed is also 0, or 100% if Driven Wheel Speed > 0.
For All Wheel Drive cars, it is calculated as (fastest wheel speed - slowest wheel speed) * 100% / slowest wheel speed. If slowest wheel speed is 0, it will show 0% if fastest wheel speed is also 0, or 100% if fastest wheel speed > 0.

6785.L: REM Digital Pulse Output 4 Active Time
6785.d: The active time of the signal put out on the REM DPO 4 pin.

6786.L: REM Digital Pulse Output 4 Safe State
6786.d:
Allows the user to select the Safe State for DPO4 to be either "Active" or "Inactive" if there is an error with the Race Expansion Module; such as loss in communications with the ECU.
	Active - The ECU will activate the output when there is an error. Please check that the Active State has been configured correctly. A thermo-fan is an example of something which should have Active safe state.
	Inactive - The ECU will not activate the output when there is an error. Please check that the Active State has been configured correctly.
	eg. if we are controlling a thermofan relay; which is switched on when the Active State is Low; we would want the fan to be ON if there is an error. Therefore; the Safe State would be Active.
	Alternatively; if we have a Nitrous Solenoid; which is switched on when the Active State is Low; we would want the solenoid to be OFF if there is an error. Therefore; the Safe State would be Inactive.

6790.L: REM Digital Pulse Output 5 Active State
6790.d:
The logic level of the output when it is active (on). The other option becomes the inactive state logic level.

		Low = Driven to 0 Volts. Current Limit: 1 Amp.
		High = Pulled to Pull Up Voltage through a 4k7 Ohm resistor.
	
If output is active (output is 'on'):
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 1.

If output is Inactive (output is 'off'):
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 1.

If your load is connected between a positive voltage source (e.g. battery 12V) and the ECU:
* Active State is usually 0.
* This is sometimes called Low Side Drive or Ground Side Drive or Cold Side Switching.
* This is the most common drive type in EFI systems.

If your load is connected between Ground and the ECU:
* This can only be controlled by DPOs which allow High Side drive or Both.
* Active State is usually 1.
* This is sometimes called High Side Drive or Hot Side Switching.
* This is common in cars which weren't designed for EFI.
* This is used for Honda VTEC.

7063.d:
How to combine conditions.
And: The combined result will be true if both individual conditions are true.
Or: The combined result will be true if at least one individual condition is true.
Note that if you have 3 conditions enabled: And gets evaluated before Or.
e.g. Cond 1 And  Cond 2 Or Cond 3:
    Cond 1 And Cond 2 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 3.
e.g. Cond 1 OR Cond 2 AND Cond 3:
    Cond 2 And Cond 3 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 1.
If both combiners are the same (e.g. both And or both Or): then the order doesn't matter.

7404.d:
The Nitrous stage can be activated many different ways. 
All Activation Methods can also have a master 'Enable' switch - see 'Enable Settings'.
All Activation Methods also require the General enabling conditions to be met. 
As well as the General Conditions being met and master Enable being on, the Activation Mode adds another condition:

Always Active - General enabling conditions only. 

Race Timer - The Race Timer value is greater than or equal to the value in the Activation table. 

Vehicle Speed - The Vehicle Speed is greater than or equal to the value in the Activation table. 

Trans Brake On - Trans Brake State channel is Active or Bump/Creep.

Trans Brake Off - Trans Brake State channel is Inactive.

Clutch Switch Off - Clutch Switch Input State channel is Off (0).

Clutch Switch On - Clutch Switch Input State channel is On (1).

Launch Control Active - Launch Control Output State channel is Active.

Launch Control Inactive - Launch Control Output State channel is NOT Active. 

Launch Control Switch On - Launch Control Switch is On (1).

Launch Control Switch Off - Launch Control Switch is Off (0).

8019.d:
The maximum driveshaft RPM rate of change. This can be used to filter out spikes in driveshaft rpm that may occur with noise.

To determine a good value, open a log of a run in Haltech Data Log Viewer, right click the name of the log, click Add Math Channel and configure as follows:

Name: Derivative Driveshaft RPM
Time Operation: Differentiate
Unit Type: Engine Speed
Equation: Double click your new math channel to display it, preferably alongside driveshaft RPM, and look for the highest value of Derivative Driveshaft RPM which isn't cause by a noise spike. This will typically occur during a gear shift or at launch. Multiply by a safety factor (e.g. 1.5), and use this number as your max derivative value.

8047.L: Transient Throttle Load Deceleration Dead Band
8047.d: Once a transient throttle disenrichment event is triggered, the deceleration of the load source must exceed this value to maintain disenrichment. This acts as a Decay system. For longer disenrichment periods use a low value, for shorter disenrichment periods use a larger value.

8050.d: Decel Cut will not be active below this coolant temperature. This setting is to prevent decel fuel cut from activating with a cold engine resulting in poor drivability. If you don't want coolant temp to have an effect, set to a value below normal cold start temperatures.

8056.d: Decel Cut will not arm until Engine Demand exceeds this value. It will then activate when Zero Demand conditions are met. This is to prevent oscillation around the zero demand conditions. If you don't want Engine Demand to have an effect, set to 0. Typically values are around 1 to 5%.

Select when the Home sensor should be used.
Always - Always uses the Home signal to determine engine position information unless RPM falls below the Minimum RPM setting (if enabled).
Until Full Sync - When this is set to Until Full Sync the home signal gets ignored once the ECU has been at full cycle engine synchronisation for 8 engine cycles. After this only the crank sensor is used for engine position information. This is only available for some triggers.

8254.d: This is the percentage of cylinders to be cut in order to limit engine RPM for the Aux Rev Limiter.

8264.d:
The Aux Rev Limiter adder value. This changes the pattern in which cylinders are cut.

Small numbers (e.g. 10) clump the cuts together to form bigger bangs. Middle sized numbers (e.g. 105; 151) spread the cut events smoothly. Large numbers (e.g. 240) have the same effect as smaller numbers. When this value is set to 0 a default value will be used that results in smooth cuts.

Suggested method for Adder Value selection is to start with a value of 100, and lower the number for rougher cuts or increase the number for smoother cuts. Suggested values can be found in the Help.

Selects the method that the stepper motor will calibrate. The calibration is required because a stepper motor idle valve does not have a position sensor to report where it is.
Normal calibration fully closes the stepper during calibration.
Reverse calibration fully opens the stepper during calibration.
If the engine is started while the stepper is still calibrating, the engine will initially idle low for Normal calibration or high for Reverse calibration.

8336.d: Because the home signal pulses have to come in between Trigger pulses and/or events (such as the first tooth after a missing gap) there is a limited range of where the home pulses can come in. This channel shows where the home pulses are coming in relative to the maximum valid range. If this reaches 0% or 100% the trigger system will desynchronise and your engine will likely miss and the ECU may start firing ignition at the wrong time. If your engine is playing up and this reads close to 0% or 100% this may be the problem.

8338.d:
Delay between releasing the trans-brake input and releasing the trans-brake output

The trans brake delay function allows for a programmed delay of the trans-brake release. This is to help prevent a negative Reaction Time (i.e. a "Red Light" start) in drag racing applications by adding a programmable delay to the release of the trans brake.

For this to be effective the ECU MUST have control over the Trans brake relay and the Trans Brake Button MUST NOT Interrupt power to the Trans Brake Relay.

8436.d:
The type of cut applied by the auxiliary RPM limiter.
 * Hard Cut - An aggressive rpm limiter. All cylinders are cut at the defined RPM Limit and resume operation when the RPM has fallen below the RPM Limit value by the Hysterisis amount.
 * Soft Cut - A softer rpm limiter. Individual cylinders are cut evenly to maintain RPM at or below the RPM Limit.
 * Cut Off - A user defined rpm limiter. A user definable percentage cut with user definable cut pattern (determined by the Adder Value) is used, resulting in smoother or rougher cuts as requested. This can change the sound of the RPM limiter.

8553.d:
The ignition timing correction to apply when a torque reduction or limit is active. 
This table should have at least one axis as Torque Reduction Total or Torque Reduction Percentage.
The Ignition Correction and Cut Percentage tables are both active at the same time. Ignition Correction gives smoother engine running and is recommended for small torque reductions. Cut Percentage is more effective for large torque reductions.
To tune this table:
* Fully tune your engine first. The Engine Torque table should also be tuned before the Ignition Correction or Cut Percentage tables.
* ensure your dyno is calculating engine torque appropriately. If tuning on a chassis dyno: set wheel size; final drive ratio; and gear ratio appropriately. This table cannot be accurately road tuned.
* Use the Temporary Torque Reduction or Temporary Torque Limit to cause a torque reduction to take place.
* Tune the Ignition Correction and Cut Percentage tables so that the dyno shows that the torque has reduced by the same amount as commanded in the Temporary Torque Reduction.

8806.d:
What functionality is associated with this button. 

Unused: Any unneeded button should be set to Unused.

Rest Position: Used to distinguish between an invalid input and no input. Calibrate this when no inputs are pressed/selected.

Enable: If state is Disabled it is changed to Ready

Disable: Cruise control state is set to Disabled.

Cancel:	If state is Cruising: Cruise Control is paused by setting state to Ready.

Set: The current speed is set as the target speed; and if Cruise Control state is Ready: it is changed to Cruising

Accel: If state is Cruising: Holding the button causes the car to accelerate until the button is released. At that point the target speed is set to the new current speed.
Max Control System Error and PID gains are the most significant factors affecting acceleration rate while holding the Accel input.

Coast: If state is Cruising: Holding the button causes the car to coast until the button is released. At that point the target speed is set to the new current speed.

+/-: If state is Cruising: A short press increases/decreases the target speed by the value of the Speed +/- Increment setting.

Resume: If state is Ready: changes to Cruising and sets the target speed to the last valid target speed. Note that this does nothing if the user hasn't pressed Set since key on.

For more information on combinations of buttons; see Help document

8810.d:
Derivative gain of 1000 takes away 1% throttle per 1 km/h speed increase per second.
Higher D gain takes away more throttle so that P and I gains can be higher before the controller becomes unstable.
Caution: High D gain when close to target can lead to subtle hunting which can cause motion sickness. data

8812.d:
Why the Cruise Control won't enable.

This is a bit-field so multiple reasons can be combined. Use a Number Display or List Display in NSP to get the list of reasons to show.

To decode from a data log: find the biggest value in the following list which is less than or equal to your Disable Reason channel. This is one of the reasons. Now subtract that number from the channel value and repeat until you get 0.
0 = Not disabled
1 = Too Slow
2 = Too Fast
4 = Brake On
8 = Clutch In
16 = Neutral
32 = Reverse
64 = Gear Not Forward
128 = Selector Not Forward
256 = Engine Limiter
512 = Engine Protection
1024 = DBW Throttle
2048 = Wheel Speed Difference

e.g. 260:
The highest value that's less than or equal is 256. 
So Engine Limiter is one reason. 
Now subtract 256 and you get 4.
The highest value that's less than or equal is 4. 
So Brake On is another reason. 
Now subtract 4 and you get 0. 
If you get non-zero: continue the process of subtracting until you reach 0. Though you usually don't need the full list.

8869.d:
The amount of air mass flow as a percentage of ideal.
Ideal is the mass of air which would be drawn in if the volumetric efficiency was 100%, air temperature was 25 degrees Celcius, and air pressure was 101.3 kPa.
Full throttle on a naturally aspirated engine will typically give values between 90% and 100%.
Forced induction engines will have values above 100% when on boost.
Hotter charge air reduces air density, so the normalised air flow decreases.
As such, the Auto V.E. Air Temp Compensation should be turned on for V.E. tuning.

8872.d: Current Idle Control Throttle Follower output. This will always be moving toward the target. When above the target; the decay table will be used to gradually close the idle valve.

8873.d: The Throttle Follower smooths the transition from open throttle to closed throttle. This is done by increasing the idle output based on the amount of rpm and load the engine is using and decaying it away as the throttle is closed. It is typically mapped to have a larger amount when either rpm or load is increased. Note that the decay time is used whenever the value is decreasing; typically when closing throttle.

8981.d:
The method used for traction control. The method is typically PID Control from Vehicle Speeds where the activation of traction control is determined by the amount of wheel slip occurring and the correction is tuned through PID.

Percentage Cut causes a percentage of the fuel or ignition events to be cut whenever the measured slip is greater than the target slip. The percentage of events cut is read from the Traction Control Percentage Cut table.

If the vehicle has a supported CAN-based unit which transmits a requested engine torque limit; you can use Vehicle CAN torque limit if you prefer.
The CAN method uses the maximum limit sent to the Haltech ECU to generate a reduction request based on how much torque the engine is currently generating. This reduction request is acted upon in your Torque Model Ignition Correction and Cut Percentage tables as any reduction request would be.

8995.d:
State of the trans-brake
Inactive (0): Trans-brake output is off. This includes when trans-brake input is ON but the output remains OFF due to enable conditions.
Active (1): Trans-brake output is on because the Trans Brake Input is on and it is not currently 'bumping' or 'creeping'.
Bump (2): Trans-brake output is briefly off in order to allow the vehicle to 'bump' forward. 
Creep (3): Trans-brake output is pulsing to allow the vehicle to 'creep' forward. 
Delay (4): Trans-brake output is held on after the trans-brake input has been released. This will be released after the Delay time has passed.
Reverse (-1): Trans-brake output is on because 'On In Reverse' is enabled and the Selector Position is Reverse.

9035.d:
The method for controlling the progressive nitrous timer. If this timer is used as an axis of the N2O Solenoid Duty Cycle table it allows for control of how progressive nitrous control is resumed after a disabling condition occurs. The Timer will start when the activating conditions are met and reset if the conditions are not. Once started, if the Throttle Position is no longer greater than the minimum, then depending on the selected mode the timer will:
* Resume - The Timer will continue to run in the background whilst the output is off.
* Hold - The Timer will pause whilst the output is off and only resume once the enabling conditions are met again.
* Reset - The Timer will reset whilst the output is off.

9050.d:
How to combine conditions. 
And: The combined result will be true if both individual conditions are true. 
Or: The combined result will be true if at least one individual condition is true.
Note that if you have 3 conditions enabled: And gets evaluated before Or. 
e.g. Cond 1 And  Cond 2 Or Cond 3:
    Cond 1 And Cond 2 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 3. 
e.g. Cond 1 OR Cond 2 AND Cond 3: 
    Cond 2 And Cond 3 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 1.
If both combiners are the same (e.g. both And or both Or): then the order doesn't matter.

9063.d:
Generic output 10 type.

 * Duty Cycle: Set the frequency to be a static value and the duty cycle is controlled using the output table.

 * Frequency: Set the Duty Cycle to be a static value and the frequency is controlled using the output table.

 * State: Set the output to be a state output. State is set by the table. Min Off Time and Min On Time can be set.

 * Current: Configure the output to be current controlled. Target current is the output of the table as a percentage of the maximum current setting of the pin in the wiring page, e.g. 0%-100% of table output is equivalent to 0 amp to Maximum Current setting of the pin.

 * 4-Wire Stepper Position (%): Configure output to control a 4 wire stepper motor. Table output is a target position based on max steps.

 * 6-Wire Stepper Position (%): Configure output to control a 6 wire stepper motor. Table output is a target position based on max steps.

9198.d:
Enables the gear ratio calculations.
Current Gear Ratio is calculated using the best guess of transmission input shaft speed and output shaft speed. 
If you enable the Transmission Input RPM sensor, then that will be used as the input shaft speed. 
Otherwise Engine RPM will be used. 
Transmission Input RPM is better, as it is assumed to be after the clutch or torque converter.

Output shaft speed primarily uses the Vehicle Speed Drive Train sensor, if that is available. 
If not, it will use the average of all driven wheel speed sensors which aren't flagged as an error. 
If no driven wheel speed sensors are available and/or functional, it will use the Vehicle Speed channel.

In order of priority:
If one or both shaft speeds are in error, Current Gear Ratio will read as Error in source channel.
If output shaft speed is stopped (0 km/h / 0 mph) and the input shaft is spinning at least 200 RPM, Current Gear Ratio be 0, as the transmission must be in Neutral.
If one or both shaft speeds are stopped, Current Gear Ratio will set to Condition Not Met.
If none of the above specific conditions are met, then Current Gear Ratio will be calculated as Input Shaft Speed / Output Shaft Speed.

9288.d:
Prevents jittery on / off behaviour by applying this hysteresis when passing a threshold value with decreasing RPM. Does not change behaviour when passing thresholds with increasing RPM. Recommended value of about 200 for most applications.
	Example 1: With an on threshold of 1800 RPM, and hysteresis of 200 RPM, Dual Intake Runner will turn on at 1800 RPM, and turn off only at 1600 RPM.
	Example 2: With an off threshold of 3600 RPM, and hysteresis of 400 RPM, Dual Intake Runner will turn off at 3600 RPM, and only turn back on at 3200 RPM.

9365.L: Transmission Control Auto Mode Shift Point Table
9365.d:
When the Transmission Control function will chose to shift gear when in Auto Mode.
This is a special table with the left axis locked to the Transmission Control Shift Point Axis channel.
The values in the axis should be configured for all gear shifts which the ECU will be able to initiate.
A normal 4 speed gearbox would have 1->2 2->1 2->3 3->2 3->4 and 4->3.
An up-shift will occur when the Shift Point Variable is greater than or equal to the value of the shift from current gear to one higher.
A down-shift will occur when the Shift Point Variable is less than or equal to the value of the shift from current gear to one lower.

When to shift down from 6th gear to 5th gear. The ECU will initiate a down-shift if the Shift Point Variable is less than or equal to this value.

9425.d:

9426.d:

Note that there are some conditions which will prevent a shift even if the engine RPM meets the RPM shift point.

9427.L: Torque Converter Lock Minimum Race Time
9427.d: The torque converter is only allowed to lock when Race Time is greater than or equal to this value. Requires Race Timer to be enabled.

9431.d: Force the torque converter to be unlocked while a gear change is in progress. Requires Gear Detection to be enabled.

9432.d:
The frequency of the Torque Converter Lock PWM output.
Sample Value:
GM 4L60-E uses 32 Hz.

9433.d: How long since the ECU started trying to lock the torque converter. Commonly used as an axis to the Torque Converter Lock Duty Cycle table to gradually lock the torque converter.

9434.L: Torque Converter Lock Duty Cycle When Unlocked
9434.d:
The duty cycle to output on the Torque Converter Lock PWM output when the Torque Converter is unlocked.
Typically 0%.
GM 4L60-E transmission uses 90% for this setting from factory.

9436.d: The torque converter is only allowed to lock in this gear or higher. Requires Gear Detection.

9437.d:
This is a special gear used by the Transmission Control function to look up RPM-based shift points.
It does NOT reflect the current state of the ECU; so is unlikely to be useful for data analysis.

9438.L: Transmission Control RPM Shift Point Table
9438.d:
When the Transmission Control function will chose to shift gear to prevent issues with over-revving the engine or stalling.
This is a special table with the left axis locked to the Transmission Control RPM Shift Point Axis channel.
The values in the axis should be configured for all gear shifts the tuner wants to have triggered by the engine RPM reaching a critical value.
An up-shift will occur when the engine RPM is greater than or equal to the value of the shift from current gear to one higher.
A down-shift will occur when the engine RPM is less than or equal to the value of the shift from current gear to one lower.

9439.d: Enables Dyno Mode when the Driven Wheel Speed is greater than or equal to the Dyno Mode Minimum Speed.

9440.d:
If Dyno Mode is enabled the Transmission Control function will go into Dyno Mode when the Driven Wheel Speed is greater than or equal to the Dyno Mode Entry Speed.
There are 3 ways to exit Dyno Mode: 
- When Driven Wheel Speed is less than or equal to the Dyno Mode Exit Speed.
- Disable Dyno Mode.
- Put the Gear Selector into Neutral. 

You will still need to disable Dyno Mode when finished on the dyno.

When in Dyno Mode the Transmission Control function will shift gears to get to the Dyno Mode Gear and lock the Torque Converter.

Drive-shaft RPM and Drive-shaft speed are common for cars with Torque Converters
Drag cars commonly use Race Time to avoid shifting due to brief wheel slip.

9455.d:
This table is used to prevent shifts which could cause problems.
If a shift isn't in the Axis 2 values; it won't be prevented.
e.g. If you want to prevent up-shifting too early in a drag race you could have shift inhibit points for 1->2 2->3 etc but not for 3->2.

Down-shift points are taken as the maximum value of the Shift Inhibit Variable Value to allow that down-shift.
e.g. You might set the shift inhibit for the 2->1 down-shift to 60 km/h to prevent over-revving the engine when in 1st gear.

Up-shift points are taken as the minimum value of the Shift Inhibit Variable Value to allow that up-shift.
e.g. You might set the shift inhibit for the 1->2 up-shift to 1.3 seconds of Race Time to prevent an up-shift occurring too early if there is wheel spin which causes the Shift Point to be reached.

This is a special table with the left axis locked to the Transmission Control Potential Shift channel.
The values in the axis should be configured for all gear shifts which the ECU will be able to initiate.
A normal 4 speed gearbox would have 1->2 2->1 2->3 3->2 3->4 and 4->3.

This equals (Line Pressure Target - Line Pressure) * P Gain / 1000 when Line Pressures are in kPa.

9495.d:
The maximum gear allowed to be shifted into by the Transmission Control function.
This is based off the Gear Detection Selector Position.
If an overdrive position is available: only Overdrive can select top gear and Drive will be able to select the second highest gear. Otherwise Drive can select top gear.
Max gear for Sport is the same as Drive.
Max gear in Low is one less than it would be for Drive.
Max gear for Manual is top gear.

Set to 0% if you just want to rely on the Lock Point Table.

Set to 0% if you just want to rely on the Lock Point Table.

9502.L: Sequential Twin Turbo Charge Relief Offset
9502.d:
When to open the Charge Relief Valve relative to the Exhaust Valve and/or Charge Valve. 
It will open at a threshold this many RPM lower than the Secondary On RPM and close again when this many RPM lower than the Secondary Off RPM.  
The Charge Relief Valve is also closed when the Exhaust Valve and/or Charge Valve are opened. 
e.g. Charge Relief Offset = 1000rpm; Secondary On RPM = 4000rpm; Secondary Off RPM = 3500rpm; 
While RPM is increasing: the Charge Relief Valve will open at 3000rpm and close at 4000rpm. 
While RPM is decreasing: the Charge Relief Valve will open at 3500rpm and close at 2500rpm.
This is useful to prevent the secondary turbo from surging while the Pre-Control is active. 
Typical value 1000 or less. Default is an overly conservative value to prevent damage.

9506.d:
Installed - Select this option when the vehicle has a factory ABS installed and operational.

Not Installed (simulate for ZF transmission) - Select this option when a ZF automatic transmission is being used in a conversion, and the Ford Falcon factory ABS module is not installed in the vehicle.
			
This feature will allow automatic shifting of the ZF transmission without an ABS module present, however may not fully replicate factory behaviour in every application. Please verify correct transmission functionality in each installation.
Do not use this mode if the Ford Falcon factory ABS unit is present and functional in the vehicle as CAN communication conflicts will occur.
In this mode, you can still use the Drive Train Vehicle Speed Sensor as a CAN bus Input for your vehicle speed source. You will need to calibrate (Vehicle Speed Sensors -> Calibration tab) to ensure vehicle speed accuracy.

9568.d:
The state of the output.

1 = Active. Output level matches the Active State setting.
0 = Inactive. Output level is opposite the Active State setting.

9570.d: The active time of the output.

9571.d:
The logic level of the output when it is active (on). The other option becomes the inactive state logic level.

		Low = Driven to 0 Volts. Current Limit: 1 Amp.
		High = Pulled to Pull Up Voltage Setting through a 4K7 Ohm resistor.
	
If output is active (output is 'on'):
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 1.

If output is Inactive (output is 'off'):
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 1.

If your load is connected between a positive voltage source (e.g. battery 12V) and the ECU:
* Active State is usually 0.
* This is sometimes called Low Side Drive or Ground Side Drive or Cold Side Switching.
* This is the most common drive type in EFI systems.

If your load is connected between Ground and the ECU:
* This can only be controlled by DPOs which allow High Side drive or Both.
* Active State is usually 1.
* This is sometimes called High Side Drive or Hot Side Switching.
* This is common in cars which weren't designed for EFI.
* This is used for Honda VTEC.

10213.L: Nitrous Stage 1 Throttle Lift/Pedal Resume Delay
10213.d:
If the driver lifts (pedals) and then re-applies throttle while the activation conditions are still met, the stage will wait this time before re-activating. 
It is recommended to set the Throttle Lift/Pedal Resume Delay to a different value in each stage. This will prevent all stages from re-activating simultaneously; which could damage the engine.
If no delay is desired this setting can be left at 0.

10474.L: Transmission Control Flat Shift Link Option
10474.d:
Many automatic transmissions and sequential dog-boxes require torque reduction and/or throttle blip some time during the shift process.
This allows the Transmission Control function to request a torque reduction and/or throttle blip from the Flat Shift function.
In some cases the torque reduction and throttle blip should start before the gear shift actuators are triggered and sometimes the shift actuators should start first.
This setting allows the tuner to select which actions are taken and whether they are before or after the shift actuators have been turned on.
