10487.d:
Whether the Transmission Control function is allowed to skip gears. e.g. go straight from 4th to 2nd.
There are two ways the transmission controller will decide to skip gears:
* If the Paddle Shift Stack has more than one shift stacked.
* If the Shift Point Variable is Driveshaft RPM; Driveshaft Vehicle Speed; Driven Wheel Speed or Race Time AND the shift point tables indicate that more than one shift is needed.
  This happens if the Shift Point Variable is high enough that a new shift would be requested straight away after a shift is complete.
  e.g. Car is in 1st gear; Driven Wheel Speed is 40km/h; 1->2 up-shift point is 20km/h and 2->3 up-shift point is 30km/h. This circumstance can occur if the drive moves the Gear Selector from 1 to D.
  Note that Auto-shift does NOT skip gears if the Shift Variable is set to Engine RPM. This is because the shift itself would lower the Engine RPM so the ECU cannot determine whether another shift will be required.

Sequential transmissions obviously cannot skip gears.
Some conventional automatic transmissions may not shift as well when skipping gears. It's possible that some transmissions will be damaged by skipping gears.

10488.d:
Whether to enable an additional shift point table based off engine RPM.
This table is active even when Gear Selector is in Manual. This allows automatic up-shifts just before redline and automatic down-shifts just before the engine reaches too low RPM to operate well.

10702.d:
Generic output 11 type.

 * Duty Cycle: Set the frequency to be a static value and the duty cycle is controlled using the output table.

 * Frequency: Set the Duty Cycle to be a static value and the frequency is controlled using the output table.

 * State: Set the output to be a state output. State is set by the table. Min Off Time and Min On Time can be set.

 * Current: Configure the output to be current controlled. Target current is the output of the table as a percentage of the maximum current setting of the pin in the wiring page, e.g. 0%-100% of table output is equivalent to 0 amp to Maximum Current setting of the pin.

 * 4-Wire Stepper Position (%): Configure output to control a 4 wire stepper motor. Table output is a target position based on max steps.

 * 6-Wire Stepper Position (%): Configure output to control a 6 wire stepper motor. Table output is a target position based on max steps.

10767.d:
This selects which method is used to prevent accidental shifts to Neutral while driving.

None. Paddles only select forward gears : 
Paddles do not allow shifting to Neutral or Reverse. 
This should be selected when there is another method of selecting Neutral. 
e.g. an automatic transmission T-bar. 

Hold paddle for Neutral : 
The driver must hold the shift paddle for the Paddles Neutral/Reverse Shift Hold Time in order to perform a restricted shift.

Hold neutral lock-out and tap paddle : 
The driver must hold a Neutral Lock-out switch in order to perform a restricted shift.
Some sequential transmissions have a mechanical lock-out. If your transmission has one; it is suggested to wire a switch from the mechanical lock-out to the ECU in order to prevent the pneumatic system from attempting a shift which could damage the mechanical lock-out.

Note that these are the restricted shifts:
- First to Neutral
- Neutral to First
- Neutral to Reverse

e.0: None. Paddles only select forward gears
e.2: Hold neutral lock-out and tap paddle

10971.d:
How to combine conditions. 
And: The combined result will be true if both individual conditions are true. 
Or: The combined result will be true if at least one individual condition is true.
Note that if you have 3 conditions enabled: And gets evaluated before Or. 
e.g. Cond 1 And  Cond 2 Or Cond 3:
    Cond 1 And Cond 2 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 3. 
e.g. Cond 1 OR Cond 2 AND Cond 3: 
    Cond 2 And Cond 3 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 1.
If both combiners are the same (e.g. both And or both Or): then the order doesn't matter.

11149.d:
This overrides the normal shift duration when a motorbike style sequential transmission is attempting to shift into Neutral.
This is required because Neutral is half way between 1st and 2nd gear; requiring special actuator behaviour to select the gear. The ECU only attempts to shift to Neutral when coming from 1st gear.
Note that there isn't a guarantee that the gearbox will actually be put into Neutral. The transmission can end up in 2nd gear if the pulse is too long or stay in 1st if the pulse is too short.
It is important for the driver to hold the clutch until they have confirmation that Neutral was successfully achieved (Neutral light or gear display).

11243.d:
How to combine conditions. 
And: The combined result will be true if both individual conditions are true. 
Or: The combined result will be true if at least one individual condition is true.
Note that if you have 3 conditions enabled: And gets evaluated before Or. 
e.g. Cond 1 And  Cond 2 Or Cond 3:
    Cond 1 And Cond 2 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 3. 
e.g. Cond 1 OR Cond 2 AND Cond 3: 
    Cond 2 And Cond 3 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 1.
If both combiners are the same (e.g. both And or both Or): then the order doesn't matter.

11747.d:
Optionally allow one or both shift paddles to ignore the Shift Inhibit table.
Note that if Block Down Shift Over-Rev is enabled; paddle shift requests can still be blocked to prevent engine damage.

Paddles Obey Inhibit: This is the safest option.
Up Paddle Ignores Inhibit: Commonly used in drag racing applications where the up shift inhibit is set to Race Time. Choosing this option allows the driver to request up shifts either to select a higher gear for a burn out; or for pre-race testing of the shifter actuation.
Down Paddle Ignores Inhibit: No known application. Added for the sake of completeness.
Paddles Ignore Inhibit: Gives the driver full control. But the driver must be aware of the dangers of down shifting while the vehicle is travelling too fast.
Recommended Value: Paddles Obey Inhibit.

Note that this will update even if shift inhibits prevent a shift from occuring. The Transmission Control Shift Inhibit Status channel can be used to determine why a shift doesn't occur.
For logging purposes:
0 = None
1 = Gear Selector Position
2 = Main Auto Shift Point
3 = RPM Shift Point
4 = Paddles
5 = Dyno Mode
6 = Shift To First
7 = Spool Up Gear
8 = Selector Position Max Gear

11749.L: Liberty Transmission Fork Saver Min TPS
11749.s: Lib Trans Fork Sav Min TPS
11749.d:
The transmission outputs will only be on when TPS is greater than or equal to the Fork Saver TPS Limit AND/OR the Driveshaft RPM is less than or equal to the Fork Saver Driveshaft RPM Limit.
Gear outputs are active when DS RPM is below the threshold regardless of TPS.
Gear outputs are active when DS RPM is above the threshold and TPS is also above the threshold.
Gear outputs are inactive when DS RPM is above the threshold and TPS is below the threshold.

Typical values: 5% TPS and 10 RPM. This will allow you to select a gear while stationary and up-shifting will happen as normal when on throttle.

Some Liberty transmissions have ramped gear engagement dogs which allow for zero shift time during up-shifts - which is perfect for drag racing when everything goes well.
But when the driver releases the throttle (because they have to pedal the car or when crossing the finish line) these ramped dogs force the gear to be disengaged.
If this happens while a pneumatic solenoid is trying to hold it in gear then parts can break.
The Fork Saver TPS Limit and Fork Saver Driveshaft RPM Limit can prevent this from happening by disabling the transmission control outputs when the car is travelling at speed and the engine is no longer accelerating the car.

11750.L: Liberty Transmission Fork Saver Max Driveshaft RPM
11750.s: Lib Trans Fork Sav Max DSRPM
11750.d:
The transmission outputs will only be on when TPS is greater than or equal to the Fork Saver TPS Limit AND/OR the Driveshaft RPM is less than or equal to the Fork Saver Driveshaft RPM Limit.
Gear outputs are active when DS RPM is below the threshold regardless of TPS.
Gear outputs are active when DS RPM is above the threshold and TPS is also above the threshold.
Gear outputs are inactive when DS RPM is above the threshold and TPS is below the threshold.

Typical values: 5% TPS and 10 RPM. This will allow you to select a gear while stationary and up-shifting will happen as normal when on throttle.

Some Liberty transmissions have ramped gear engagement dogs which allow for zero shift time during up-shifts - which is perfect for drag racing when everything goes well.
But when the driver releases the throttle (because they have to pedal the car or when crossing the finish line) these ramped dogs force the gear to be disengaged.
If this happens while a pneumatic solenoid is trying to hold it in gear then parts can break.
The Fork Saver TPS Limit and Fork Saver Driveshaft RPM Limit can prevent this from happening by disabling the transmission control outputs when the car is travelling at speed and the engine is no longer accelerating the car.

11816.d:
What to use to add extra air to the engine intake. This is optional. 
- Drive By Wire Minimum uses the Drive by Wire throttle to increase airflow into the engine. 
  This method uses the Intake Air Addition table to determine the minimum throttle opening to use. This allows other functions such as throttle blip to cause the throttle to open more than the antilag amount. 
  This is typically used in DBW applications. 
- Throttle Bypass Valve should be selected when a dedicated valve is installed to bypass the throttle body in order to increase airflow on cable throttle applications. 
- Idle Control Minimum or Idle Control Offset should be chosen if an existing Idle Control valve is opened more to allow additional air to flow into the engine.

11861.L: Water Injection Advanced Progressive Control Mode
11861.d:
The method for controlling the progressive water injection timer. If this timer is used as an axis of the water injection output duty cycle table it allows for control of how progressive water injection control is resumed after a disabling condition occurs. The Timer will start when the activating conditions are met and reset if the conditions are not. Once started, if the enabling conditions are not met then depending on the selected mode the timer will:
* Resume - The Timer will continue to run in the background whilst the output is off.
* Hold - The Timer will pause whilst the output is off and only resume once the enabling conditions are met again. 
* Reset - The Timer will reset whilst the output is off.

11866.d:
The Water Injection can be activated many different ways. 
All Activation Methods can also have a master 'Enable' switch - see 'Enable Settings'.
All Activation Methods also require the General enabling conditions to be met. 
As well as the General Conditions being met and master Enable being on, the Activation Mode adds another condition:

Always Active - General enabling conditions only. 

Race Timer - The Race Timer value is greater than or equal to the value in the Activation table. 

Vehicle Speed - The Vehicle Speed is greater than or equal to the value in the Activation table. 

Trans Brake On - Trans Brake State channel is Active or Bump/Creep.

Trans Brake Off - Trans Brake State channel is Inactive.

Clutch Switch Off - Clutch Switch Input State channel is Off (0).

Clutch Switch On - Clutch Switch Input State channel is On (1).

Launch Control Active - Launch Control Output State channel is Active.

Launch Control Inactive - Launch Control Output State channel is NOT Active. 

Launch Control Switch On - Launch Control Switch is On (1).

Launch Control Switch Off - Launch Control Switch is Off (0).

11873.L: Water Injection Advanced Target AFR Correction Enable
11873.d: Enables target AFR correction for Water Injection Advanced.

11874.L: Water Injection Advanced Progressive Control Enable
11874.d: Control Water injection output duty cycle

11875.d: The output state of the Water Injection Advanced

11880.L: Water Injection Advanced Target AFR Correction
11880.d:
This value will be ADDED to the target AFR table, For example:
Lambda:
1.00 + -0.03 = 0.97
AFR-p:
14.7 + -0.5 = 14.2
Pay special attention to the - and +

11882.L: Water Injection Advanced Solenoid Duty Cycle
11882.d: This table outputs a duty cycle for the water injection output.

11883.d: Water Injection Advanced Progressive Timer will be controlled by the enabling conditions of the progressive control mode. It is recommended to use this channel for the Water Injection Advanced Solenoid Duty Cycle table

11884.d:
Enables the Water Injection Advanced Master Enable. 
When using the Master Enable, the Master Enable must be on with all other conditions met to activate the Water Injection Advanced function.
When not using the Master Enable, the Water Injection Advanced function will activate immediately once all other conditions are met.

11885.L: Water Injection Advanced Enable Switch Enable
11885.d: This enables a switch to control the activation/deactivation of the enable.

11886.d: Describes the switch input for Water Injection Advanced Enable

11887.L: Water Injection Advanced Enable Switch State
11887.d: This is the current state of the enable input switch.

11888.L: Water Injection Advanced Enable Output State
11888.d: The output state of the Water Injection Advanced Enable

11889.L: Water Injection Advanced Enable Conditional Enable

11890.L: Water Injection Advanced Enable Conditional Switch Operand
11890.d: The operand used to join the conditional and the switch.

11894.d: Enables the Water Injection Advanced Override. This is an optional override input which can be used to activate the Water Injection Advanced function regardless of other activation conditions and modes.

11895.L: Water Injection Advanced Override Switch Enable
11895.d: This enables a switch to control the activation/deactivation of the override.

11896.L: Water Injection Advanced Override Switch Desc
11896.d: Describes the switch input for Water Injection Advanced Override.

11897.L: Water Injection Advanced Override Switch State
11897.d: This is the current state of the override input switch.

11898.L: Water Injection Advanced Override Output State
11898.d: The output state of the Water Injection Advanced Override

11899.L: Water Injection Advanced Override Conditional Enable

11900.L: Water Injection Advanced Override Conditional Switch Operand
11900.d: The operand used to join the conditional and the switch.

11904.L: Water Injection Advanced Override Minimum Engine Running Time
11904.d: The minimum engine running time that must elapse before the Water Injection Advanced Override can be activated.

11905.L: Water Injection Advanced Override Minimum RPM
11905.d: The minimum RPM that must be achieved before the Water Injection Advanced Override can be activated.

11906.L: Water Injection Advanced Override Minimum TPS
11906.d: The minimum throttle position that must be achieved before the Water Injection Advanced Override can be activated.

12010.d:
Select how to determine if an air leak is occurring. 
Sensor Logic: The sensor uses internal logic to determine if an air leak has occurred and notifies the ECU.
Pressure Drop: Use the Pressure Drop value setting to allow the ECU to determine if an air leak is occurring.

12011.d:
If a pressure drop this value or higher is observed within a 5 second period then the Air Leak DTC is flagged.
Example - Pressure Drop is set to 1 psi. At 30 seconds front left tyre pressure is read at 35psi. At 32 seconds front left tyre pressure is read at 34psi - front left tyre air leak DTC flagged because pressure dropped 1 psi or more within a 5 second period.

12038.d:
Air Leak Detected. For the purposes of logging:
0 - No leak detected
1 - Front Left Tyre air leak
2 - Front Right Tyre air leak
4 - Rear Left Tyre air leak
8 - Rear Right Tyre air leak
Multiple air leaks detected will show up as those values added together. For example: front left and front right air leak detected will show up as '3' in the logger.

e.7: Front Left + Front Right + Rear Left
e.11: Front Left + Front Right + Rear Right
e.13: Front Left + Rear Left + Rear Right
e.14: Front Right + Rear Left + Rear Right

Sensors which are configured to use Engine Synchronous Voltage are sampled many times over a window and averaged.
Manifold Pressure is always configured to use Engine Synchronous Voltage.
Exhaust Manifold Pressure and Fuel Pressure sensors can be configured as either Engine Synchronous Voltage or simply Analogue - Voltage.
These sensors typically fluctuate throughout an engine cycle.
  - Manifold Pressure decreases during intake strokes (as air moves from the manifold into the cylinders), and increases other times (as air moves past the throttle body into the manifold). There can also be pulsation effects.
  - Exhaust Manifold Pressure increases during exhaust strokes, and decreases other times (as exhaust gases pass through the turbine).
  - Fuel Pressure tends to decrease when injectors open and increase when injectors close. There can also be pulsation effects.

This setting allows selection of how much of the engine cycle to average the sensor reading over.

1 cylinder averages the sensor reading over one cylinder period.
  - This is most responsive, but can have fluctuations on some engines (e.g. V engines with separate manifolds, engines with long intake manifolds).
  - e.g. a 4 cylinder engine will average the sensor reading over 1/4 of the engine cycle.

2 cylinders often helps smooth out some fluctuations which can be seen when set to 1 cylinder.
  - This is typically used on V engines with separate intake manifolds, or on some long inline engines.
  - e.g. an 8 cylinder engine will average the sensor reading over 1/4 of the engine cycle.
  - 2 cylinders can only be used on engines with an even number of cylinders.

Revolution uses one engine revolution.

Engine Cycle uses a full engine cycle.
  - This gives the smoothest results, at the cost of being less responsive.

Engine Cycle is the same as Revolution for Rotaries and 2 Strokes.

12212.d:
Which staging method to use. 
Nexus Style : Recommended for new installations, when the fueling hasn't been tuned yet. 
 - First stage only until it reaches Stage 1 Staging Duty Cycle. 
 - Then the first stage holds at Stage 1 Staging Duty Cycle, and the next stage starts ramping in. 
 - This is repeated for all further stages. 
 - If all stages are at their Staging Duty Cycle and more fuel is required, then all stages will increase their duty cycle up to 100%. The rate of increase may differ between stages such that all stages reach 100% duty cycle at the same time.

If Stage Flow Percentage Tables is enabled: 
 - Flow Percentage tables control how much of the total fuel usage gets injected per stage, up to the Staging Duty Cycle. 
 - Once a stage has reached its Staging Duty Cycle, the excess will be distributed to other stages instead. 
 - Once all stages reach their Staging Duty Cycle, they will all increase, possibly at different rates, so that they all reach 100% at the same time. 
 - Setting all tables to 0% results in the same behaviour as having Stage Flow Percentage Tables disabled.

Elite Style : only recommended if your fueling has already been tuned with Elite Style staging. 
 - All active stages use the same duty cycle. 
 - The number of active stages increases when the highest active stage duty cycle exceeds the Max Duty Cycle setting. 
 - The number of active stages decreases when the highest active stage duty cycle goes below the Min Duty Cycle setting. 
 - If you are going to tune the fuel, it is recommended to change to Nexus Style.

12251.d:
Enables an Acknowledge input for Engine Protection. 
When the Acknowledge input is active; all current DTCs get acknowledged for the purposes of Engine Protection and Engine Protection is reset.
If a previously acknowledged DTC passes then fails again; it will no longer be acknowledged; and will cause the Engine Protection to become activated again. It will require another Acknowledgement to clear again.
Note that if the Acknowledge input is wired to a switch; it also functions like the override. i.e. no engine protection will occur while it is on. 
Note that the DTC is still stored in memory; so the software will still show the code when connected.

Keypad Button Information:
 * The output light is on when Engine Protection is active (the Engine Protection Current Severity Level is non-zero)
 * The error light turns on if there is an error with any of the input pins being used.

12342.L: Torque Management Wheelie Control Hold Timer Duration
12342.d:
How long the wheelie hold timer runs for.
The wheelie control hold timer can only become active if the wheelie control conditions are met. 
The wheelie hold timer starts when wheelie control % cut and/or wheelie control ignition correction is non-zero.
While the wheelie hold timer is active:
  - if the % cut table reading increases or the ignition correction table reading decreases: (i.e. the wheelie is getting higher)
    - the timer gets reset
    - % cut will increase to the table reading if the table reading is higher than the current percentage cut. 
    - Ignition correction will go to the table reading if the table reading is more retarded than the current value. 
  - if the readings are going back towards 0:
    -cut % and ignition correction remain the same. 
When the timer ends:
  - if either table is non-zero, it will start again, with % cut and ignition correction equal to the current table readings. 
  - Otherwise it will stop, and the cut % and ignition corrections will go to 0.

12344.L: Torque Management Wheelie Control Only When Race Timer Running

If this is ticked and the Race Timer is stopped or greater than the Max Race Time: 
  - Wheelie Control Ignition Correction table is ignored and no correction will be used.
  - Wheelie Control Cut Percentage table is ignored and no cut percentage will be used. 
  - Wheelie Control Timer will be stopped.

12365.L: Cam Control Switched Intake RPM Hysteresis
12365.d:
Prevents jittery on / off behaviour by applying this hysteresis when passing a threshold value with decreasing RPM. Does not change behaviour when passing thresholds with increasing RPM. Recommended value of about 200 for most applications.
	Example 1: With an on threshold of 1800 RPM, and hysteresis of 200 RPM, Cam Control Switched output will turn on at 1800 RPM, and turn off only at 1600 RPM.
	Example 2: With an off threshold of 3600 RPM, and hysteresis of 400 RPM, Cam Control Switched output will turn off at 3600 RPM, and only turn back on at 3200 RPM.

12456.d:
The state of the Front Windscreen Washer controller.
	For data-logging purposes:
		-5 = Low Input Error
		-4 = Output Error
		-3 = Request Input Error
		-2 = Level Low
		-1 = Input Off
		 0 = Function Disabled
		 1 = On

12457.d:
Why the Cruise Control has been shut down.
Note that the Cruise Control Disable Reason channel is normally the first thing to check if the Cruise Control has turned off unexpectedly.

e.1: Cruise Control function running when disabled
e.5: Cruise Control Checker couldnt read the controller target speed
e.6: Target Speed is not between target and current speeds
e.7: Target Speed outside min and max speeds
e.8: Brake or Clutch or Neutral Switch on and Cruise Control hasn't cancelled
e.9: Driven Wheel speed is outside min and max speeds
e.10: Target speed is outside min and max speeds
e.11: Output is outside min and max limits
e.12: Engine Limiter or Percentage Cut active
e.14: Conditions are OK but theres a Disable Reason
e.15: Target Speed changed while state is cruising
e.16: Output Timeout expired by the output is still on
e.17: Input shows unused while the state is accelerate or decelerate
e.18: Input State is reading Unused for too long
e.19: A long press is being ignored
e.20: cancel or disable button is being ignored
e.21: state is accelerate or decelerate but a button isnt being held
e.22: Cruise Control Input function not running
e.24: State or Target Speed channels out of sync
e.25: Selector Position not a forward gear
e.26: Gear Detection not a forward gear

14057.d:
The current state the wastegate is in. This should help to diagnose issues.
-25 = Uncalibrated - Needs Calibration
-24 = Uncalibrated - One or more settings is invalid
-23 = Uncalibrated - Output Error while calibrating
-22 = Uncalibrated - Failed while calibrating second limit
-21 = Uncalibrated - Failed while calibrating first limit.
-20 = Uncalibrated - Position Sensor out of range.

-4 = Overheated! Parking Open. The Wastegate 2 Temperature Sensor shows a problem; so the wastegate is being parked 90% open. 
-5 = Overheated! Parked Open. The Wastegate 2 Temperature Sensor shows a problem; so the wastegate has been parked 90% open. 
    This can be a temperature >= 150 degC (302 degF). 
    It could be an I/O error (e.g. unassigned pin). 
    It could be that the input voltage is out of bounds (less than 0.1V or greater than 4.9V).

e.-24: Uncalibrated - One or more settings is invalid
e.-22: Uncalibrated - Failed while calibrating second limit
e.-21: Uncalibrated - Failed while calibrating first limit
e.-20: Uncalibrated - Position Sensor out of range
e.-12: Disabled - Settings Invalid. Check the software for redified settings.

14287.d: What percentage of cylinders are being cut to enforce the current RPM Limiter.

14288.d:
The total percentage of cylinders being cut. This combines the Cut Percentage (from functions such as Traction Control) and the RPM Limiter Cut Percentage.
Note that this is not simple addition. It is calculated as 100% - the number of cylinder events which occur despite both limiters.
So 100% - ( (100% - Cut%) * (100% - RPM Limiter Cut%) ).
e.g. 50% Cut Percentage and 50% RPM Limiter Cut% gives a result of 75% cut. This is because on average 25% of cylinder events will get both fuel and spark.

14397.L: RPM Limiter Cut Off RPM Range
14397.d:
Used only when the Cut Type is set to Cut Off. 
There will be 100% cut when RPM is greater than the End RPM table.
There will be 0% cut when RPM is less than (End RPM table - Cut Off RPM Range).
When RPM is between these two, the cut percentage will be linearly interpolated based off the range. 

e.g. End RPM = 4000, Cut Off Range = 500.
- When RPM  is less than 3500: 0% cut. 
- When RPM is greater than 4000: 100% cut.
- When RPM is 3750: 50% cut. 
- When RPM is 3900: 80% cut.

14398.d:
Used only when the Cut Type is set to Cut Off. 
This changes the pattern in which cylinders are cut.

When this value is set to 0 a default value will be used that results in smooth cuts.
Small numbers (e.g. 10) clump the cuts together to form bigger bangs. Middle sized numbers (e.g. 105; 151) spread the cut events smoothly. Large numbers (e.g. 240) have the same effect as smaller numbers. 

Suggested method for Adder Value selection is to start with a value of 50, and lower the number for rougher cuts or increase the number for smoother cuts.

14399.d:
Controls how the fuel or ignition limiting is performed.
 * Soft Cut - A softer rpm limiter. Individual cylinders are cut evenly to maintain RPM at or below the RPM Limit.
 * Cut Off - A user defined rpm limiter. A user definable percentage cut with user definable cut pattern (determined by the Adder Value) is used, resulting in smoother or rougher cuts as requested. This can change the sound of the RPM limiter.

14734.d:
The gear suggested by the Selector Position. 
Note that if there is only a single Selector position input: this will match Selector Max Gear. 
But when Selector Position Type is Voltage Input + Switch Inputs: this will follow the Voltage input. This allows the switch inputs to be used 
If an overdrive position is available: only Overdrive will suggest top gear and Drive will suggest the second highest gear. Otherwise Drive suggests top gear.
Suggested gear for Sport is the same as Drive.
Suggested gear in Low is one less than it would be for Drive.
Suggested gear for Manual is top gear.

15223.d:
How to combine conditions. 
And: The combined result will be true if both individual conditions are true. 
Or: The combined result will be true if at least one individual condition is true.
Note that if you have 3 conditions enabled: And gets evaluated before Or. 
e.g. Cond 1 And  Cond 2 Or Cond 3:
    Cond 1 And Cond 2 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 3. 
e.g. Cond 1 OR Cond 2 AND Cond 3: 
    Cond 2 And Cond 3 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 1.
If both combiners are the same (e.g. both And or both Or): then the order doesn't matter.

15240.L: Pit Lane Speed Limiter Cut Type
15240.d:
Method of cutting cylinders in order to control vehicle speed.
RPM Limit Calculated from Fastest Vehicle Speed: Looks at fastest vehicle speed. 
    If that is non-zero: then an RPM limit is calculated using the current engine RPM and vehicle speed. 
        RPM Limit = Speed Limit * Current RPM * 0.97 / Current Speed. 
	    This equation effectively utilises the current gear ratio. 
    If the fastest vehicle speed is 0: 
	    If you have Gear Ratios enabled: Calculates RPM Limit = Speed Limit / Ratio for 1st Gear * 0.97.
        Otherwise: No limit gets applied.
Cut Percentage Table: A cut percentage is applied using the Cut Percentage table. 
    It is advised to use the Pit Lane Speed Limiter Speed Before Cut channel as an axis. An appropriate Vehicle Speed channel can be used instead if desired.

e.1: RPM Limit Calculated from Fastest Vehicle Speed

15503.L: Boost Control Solenoid Dead Time Data

15505.d:
This channel is specifically intended for CO2 Boost Control, in order to calculate solenoid dead time.
Boost Control Solenoid Pressure Difference is calculated differently, depending on whether Boost Control is trying to increase or decrease pressure. 
When increasing pressure, the pressure difference will be the CO2 Regulator Pressure - Wastegate Pressure.
When decreasing pressure, the pressure difference will be Wastegate Pressure - Barometric Pressure (assumed to be standard atmospheric pressure if Barometric Pressure sensor is disabled)

15506.d:
When using CO2 for boost control, the ECU can compensate for solenoid dead time based off the pressure difference across the solenoid. 
Boost Control Solenoid Pressure Difference is calculated differently, depending on whether Boost Control is trying to increase or decrease pressure. 
When increasing pressure, the pressure difference will be the CO2 Regulator Pressure - Wastegate Pressure.
When decreasing pressure, the pressure difference will be Wastegate Pressure - Barometric Pressure (assumed to be standard atmospheric pressure if Barometric Pressure sensor is disabled)

15854.d:
Allows multiple gear shifts to be queued up and the shifts will take place when the Transmission Control is ready to shift. 
e.g. Driving along a straight approaching a corner. You can apply the brakes and hit the down paddle 5 times. 
The current vehicle speed might be too high to down-shift so the transmission control doesn't shift yet. 
As the vehicle speed drops low enough for a down-shift; a requested shift is taken off the Paddle Shift Stack and occurs. 
This is repeated until the Paddle Shift Stack reaches 0. 

Pressing the up shift paddle will cancel any down-shifts in the stack before adding the up-shift. 

When disabled:
  	- the stack can never go beyond one gear shift requested. 
	- if Transmission Control is enabled: paddle requests are only accepted if the Transmission Control State ends in "Normal".

16159.L: Dash Digital Pulse Output 1 Active State
16159.d:
The logic level of the output when it is active (on). The other option becomes the inactive state logic level.

		Low = Driven to 0 Volts. Current Limit: 1 Amp.
		High = Pulled to Pull Up Voltage through a 4k7 Ohm resistor.
	
If output is active (output is 'on'):
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 1.

If output is Inactive (output is 'off'):
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 1.

If your load is connected between a positive voltage source (e.g. battery 12V) and the ECU:
* Active State is usually 0.
* This is sometimes called Low Side Drive or Ground Side Drive or Cold Side Switching.
* This is the most common drive type in EFI systems.

If your load is connected between Ground and the ECU:
* This can only be controlled by DPOs which allow High Side drive or Both.
* Active State is usually 1.
* This is sometimes called High Side Drive or Hot Side Switching.
* This is common in cars which weren't designed for EFI.
* This is used for Honda VTEC.

16186.L: Dash Digital Pulse Output 4 Active State
16186.d:
The logic level of the output when it is active (on). The other option becomes the inactive state logic level.

		Low = Driven to 0 Volts. Current Limit: 1 Amp.
		High = Pulled to 12V through a 4k7 Ohm resistor.
	
If output is active (output is 'on'):
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 1.

If output is Inactive (output is 'off'):
* the output will be 1 if the Active State is 0.
* the output will be 0 if the Active State is 1.

If your load is connected between a positive voltage source (e.g. battery 12V) and the ECU:
* Active State is usually 0.
* This is sometimes called Low Side Drive or Ground Side Drive or Cold Side Switching.
* This is the most common drive type in EFI systems.

If your load is connected between Ground and the ECU:
* This can only be controlled by DPOs which allow High Side drive or Both.
* Active State is usually 1.
* This is sometimes called High Side Drive or Hot Side Switching.
* This is common in cars which weren't designed for EFI.
* This is used for Honda VTEC.

Only used with State/Switch/Button Inputs.
Single Input: Use the Input to increment the position. At max position turning the Input on will set the position back to 0.
Dual Input: Use the Down and Up Inputs to change the position. Position is clipped - that is using the Up Input at max position does nothing.

16538.d:
Only used with State/Switch/Button Inputs. This setting will only affect inputs that have indicator lights available such as Keypad buttons.
Dot: A single light will be used to show the current position.
Bar: All lights that are less than or equal to the current position will be lit up.

16539.d:

16688.d:
How to combine conditions. 
And: The combined result will be true if both individual conditions are true. 
Or: The combined result will be true if at least one individual condition is true.
Note that if you have 3 conditions enabled: And gets evaluated before Or. 
e.g. Cond 1 And  Cond 2 Or Cond 3:
    Cond 1 And Cond 2 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 3. 
e.g. Cond 1 OR Cond 2 AND Cond 3: 
    Cond 2 And Cond 3 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 1.
If both combiners are the same (e.g. both And or both Or): then the order doesn't matter.

17006.d:

17007.d:
How to combine conditions.
And: The combined result will be true if both individual conditions are true.
Or: The combined result will be true if at least one individual condition is true.
Note that if you have 3 conditions enabled: And gets evaluated before Or.
e.g. Cond 1 And  Cond 2 Or Cond 3:
    Cond 1 And Cond 2 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 3.
e.g. Cond 1 OR Cond 2 AND Cond 3:
    Cond 2 And Cond 3 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 1.
If both combiners are the same (e.g. both And or both Or): then the order doesn't matter.

17228.L: IO16 A Synced Pulse Input 4 Edge Select

Rising edge inputs require an external pull-down resistor to be fitted.

Rising = Voltage rises high to activate (eg. to 5V or 12V).

17243.L: IO16 (Box A) Half Bridge Output 0 - Active State
17243.d:
The potential pin states depend on the drive type setting:
Configure which active states exist on the pin.
Low Side: The low state is ground, the high state is open circuit (no connection).
High Side: The low state is open circuit (no connection), the high state is battery voltage.
Both: The low state is ground, the high state is battery voltage.

Setting this setting to low will make the output be in the low state when the output is on and in the high state when the output is off.  When it is set to high it is the inverse of the above.
When it is set to high it is the inverse of the above.

17322.L: IO16 (Box A) Half Bridge Output 5 Safe State
17322.d:
The pin will return to this state if the device loses connection with the ECU. What is "safe" for a pin is up to user discretion.

	For example, if the device loses connection it might be safest to turn on an output that is connected to a thermofan, where as it might be safest to turn off an output that is connected to a nitrous solenoid.

17499.L: IO16 (Box B) Half Bridge Output 0 - Active State
17499.d:
The potential pin states depend on the drive type setting:
Configure which active states exist on the pin.
Low Side: The low state is ground, the high state is open circuit (no connection).
High Side: The low state is open circuit (no connection), the high state is battery voltage.
Both: The low state is ground, the high state is battery voltage.

Setting this setting to low will make the output be in the low state when the output is on and in the high state when the output is off.  When it is set to high it is the inverse of the above.
When it is set to high it is the inverse of the above.

17755.d:
The potential pin states depend on the drive type setting:
Configure which active states exist on the pin.
Low Side: The low state is ground, the high state is open circuit (no connection).
High Side: The low state is open circuit (no connection), the high state is battery voltage.
Both: The low state is ground, the high state is battery voltage.

Setting this setting to low will make the output be in the low state when the output is on and in the high state when the output is off.  When it is set to high it is the inverse of the above.
When it is set to high it is the inverse of the above.

17930.L: Dash Digital Pulse Output 1 Safe State
17930.d:
Allows the user to select the Safe State for DPO1 to be either "Active" or "Inactive" if there is an error with the Dash; such as loss in communications with the ECU.
	Active - The ECU will activate the output when there is an error. Please check that the Active State has been configured correctly. A thermo-fan is an example of something which should have Active safe state.
	Inactive - The ECU will not activate the output when there is an error. Please check that the Active State has been configured correctly.
	eg. if we are controlling a thermofan relay; which is switched on when the Active State is Low; we would want the fan to be ON if there is an error. Therefore; the Safe State would be Active.
	Alternatively; if we have a Nitrous Solenoid; which is switched on when the Active State is Low; we would want the solenoid to be OFF if there is an error. Therefore; the Safe State would be Inactive.

The total fuel correction applied. Calculated as a percentage by comparing the fuel volume before and after all corrections have been applied. 
This includes cylinder and bank corrections, which will be averaged. 
This includes fuel flow rate corrections.

Note that for injection time tuning, this is the sum of all stage injection times. 
This can have a non-linear relationship to fuel amount if stages use different sized injectors.

18087.d:
How to combine conditions.
And: The combined result will be true if both individual conditions are true.
Or: The combined result will be true if at least one individual condition is true.
Note that if you have 3 conditions enabled: And gets evaluated before Or.
e.g. Cond 1 And  Cond 2 Or Cond 3:
    Cond 1 And Cond 2 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 3.
e.g. Cond 1 OR Cond 2 AND Cond 3:
    Cond 2 And Cond 3 gets evaluated first. Then the result of that gets Or'd with Cond 1.
If both combiners are the same (e.g. both And or both Or): then the order doesn't matter.

Transmission Control Last Shift Firmness represents the previous shift and determines how it 'felt'.
A positive number represents a firmer shift and a more negative number represents a softer shift. 0 represents a very smooth shift.

Normal

Latched

	I.e. If low speed and high speed are both on; then the state is considered to be high speed.

18843.d:
Each CAN port connects into a greater CAN Bus. The Bus Load indicates how heavily the Bus is being used. This is calculated as messages per second and displayed as a percentage, where 0% is no load and 100% is full load.
Below 50% load will produce the most reliable communications. Above 50% can result in some data being lost intermittently.

18846.L: Prevent Upshift While above User Demand Maximum
18846.d:
Prevents shifting into Overdrive gears (a gear ratio of less than 1:1 - such as 0.7:1) while at wide open throttle conditions.
This is determined by the User Demand Maximum setting under the throttle as well as the gear ratios function to determine the gear ratio of the next gear. This may result in hitting Main limiter which is more favourable than shifting into the next gear and damaging the transmission.

19000.d:
Setting to choose when the wideband sensor is running (heater enabled).

It is recommended to only run the sensor afer the engine has started, to allow moisture to be blown off the sensor before the sensor is heated up. This avoids thermal shock from the moisture evaporating suddenly on the hot sensor. This requires version 3.13.0 or later for CAN wideband controllers.

"Engine start until stopped for 30 sec" (default): The widebands will not be started until the engine has started. The widebands continue to run while the engine is running. If the engine stops while the ECU is still running, the widebands will stay on for 30 seconds. If the engine has not restarted after 30 seconds, the wideband sensors will turn off.

"Always On": The widebands will be on all the time.

"Ignition On until stopped for 30 sec": The widebands will be started when the ignition switch turns on. If, after 30 seconds, the engine has not cranked, the widebands will be shut down. Otherwise the wideband sensors will run while the engine is running, until the engine has stopped for 30 seconds or the ignition switch is off.

e.0: Engine start until stopped for 30 sec
e.2: Ignition On until stopped for 30 sec

19001.d: Off means that the ECU is commanding the wideband sensors to be off (ie, heaters not running). On means that the ECU is commanding the wideband sensors to be on (ie, heater running).

19078.d:
Alternator Control Mode.

"Custom control" is the classic alternator control function, which allows a target voltage table and base duty cycle and programmable PID gains. This controls the alternator field current through firmware, and allows for signficant customization.

"Factory control" is only support on plug-in ECUs for vehicles with an externally regulated alternator. This option uses the electronic regulator circuit within the ECU, providing for responsive control. There is no option for adjustable voltage target in this mode.
To change such a system to custom control will require rewiring the field control output to an available output (DPO, HBO etc)

19213.d:
The torque the engine would be generating if there were no friction or ignition corrections. Common names for this include Indicated Torque and Ideal Torque.
A starting point for this is to set the torque to 0 where Load - Normalised Air Mass Flow is 0.
A very rough WOT Potential Torque is about 1.2 times the torque advertised.
This table is roughly linear with Load - Normalised Air Mass Flow.

This is needed for some automatic transmissions. You may require a rough estimate in this table before you can begin tuning on some cars.
After rough configuration you can fine tune this using a dynamometer after the engine has been tuned.
